#1944. Sheffield Wednesday 0 Accrington Stanley 4: Young Owls unable to make the case in front of Dave Challinor

In what was effectively the second of two pre-season games for Dave Challinor before his league debut at home to Plymouth Argyle on Saturday, there was no real rush to put names forward.

If a Sunday evening FA Cup first-round defeat at Oldham Athletic was fairly humdrum, a Football League Trophy game watched by 5,472 hardy souls on a cold night (decide for yourself if the prefix "fool" is needed) was much more low-key, with both sides already guaranteed a place in the last 32 of this horribly bloated competition.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Between them, Wednesday's starting XI had a combined 89 league starts for the club, 75 of them belonging to captain Sean Fusire, Gabriel Otegbayo and Jarvis Thornton, none at all to Connal Trueman, Joel Akpobi and Samuel Duruh, nor Denny Oliver on his first start in any competition, or Louis Poland on his first appearance full stop.

Striker George Brown was making his first outing of an injury-hit 2026.

So there was not a great deal to take from Challinor's first Hillsborough match as Owls manager, except perhaps the fact that he lined his team up in a 3-4-3, similar to what he did at Boundary Park before changing shape in the second half there.

Nor did anyone not already in his plans make a strong case to face the Pilgrims.

Needing a point to guarantee top spot and a home draw in the last 32, the young Owls were outclassed by League Two Accrington, who claimed it instead with a 4-0 win.

Oliver put a free-kick onto the roof of the net, but otherwise the early chances fell to the visitors.

Seamus Conneely missed the target in the 18th, as did Ronan Darcy when he caught a volley sweetly quickly after.

Nigerian-born right winger Duruh, who learnt his football in Spain and has also had a loan spell with Beverley Town, beat his man in the 21st minute but his cross was cut out, albeit unconvincingly. He was the pick of the youngsters.

Two minutes later Fusire ought to have buried Akpobi's ball in from a couple of yards out, and was lucky the linesman had flagged for an earlier offence.

But that was pretty much that for Wednesday's first-half threat, barring the shot Brown made space for right at the end of it, but could not force through the defenders in front of him.

Trueman was busy in the final 15 minutes of the half, even if Alex Henderson's shot was straight at him. His next effort six minutes later forced a decent low save with strong hands.

Trueman did even better to deny Shaun Whaley in the 38th minute when the centre-forward really should have converted Henderson's ball in, but the goalkeeper got across his box well.

It was a temporary reprieve, though, Accrington taking the lead a minute later when the Owls failed to get the ball clear after Farrend Rawson struck their crossbar. Josh Smith eventually forced the ball in.

Three minutes later the lead was doubled, the ball coming in from the right to Charlie Brown to find the net from 20 yards. Good grief.

It was Brown who put a free-kick wide early in the second half before Duruh, now on the left, forced a save with a chance made by his own dribble.

It would have been three on the hour but for a big Otegbayo block on Tyler Walton, and should have been again when Darcy put an excellent chance wide.

Seven substitutes at once – three for the Owls – had added to the pre-season feel by then.

One of the later changes, Kleven de Oliveira forced a good save in the 79th minute, with Thornton doing likewise from the follow-up.

Accrington wrapped things up in the 86th minute when Wednesday were caught out trying to press the ball in midfield and it was worked down the inside-left channel for Charlie Warren to finish calmly.

Charlie Caton put the tin lid on it with a fourth goal in the fifth of seven added minutes.

It had been a forgettable night for the home side, but Saturday is when things start for real for Challinor.

Sheffield Wednesday: Trueman; Otegbayo, Weaver, McGhee (Hatfield 62); Fusire, Oliver, Thornton, Poland (de Oliveira 74); Duruh (Onoh 62), Brown (Kay HT), Akpobi (Liddell 62).

Accrington Stanley: Rogerson; Moore, Rawson (Matthews 62), J Smith; Walton (Caton 62), Conneely (Grant 62), O Smith, Brown; Darcy, Henderson (Mols 62); Whalley.

Unused substitutes: Moulden, Anderson, Warren.

#1943. Mauricio Pochettino tipped to make former Chelsea star his first Manchester United signing

Mauricio Pochettino has been tipped to sign Real Madrid defender and former Chelsea star Antonio Rudiger for Manchester United.

Pochettino is set to take charge at Old Trafford and replace Michael Carrick, who will be sacked following a dismal start to the season.

United are just 18th in the Premier League after ten games – their lowest position at this stage of a campaign since 1986.

Old Trafford bosses held a review into Carrick’s position earlier this week and appear to have decided to make a change in the dugout.

Eddie Howe, Fabian Hurzeler, Unai Emery, Antonio Conte and Julian Nagelsmann have all been linked with the Manchester United job in recent weeks.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But United chose Pochettino as their first-choice pick this week and are currently finalising a deal to bring the Argentine back to the Premier League.

Pochettino, who will step down from his role as head coach of the USA to take over at Manchester United, has already worked at fellow English clubs Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, as well as Spanish side Espanyol and French giants PSG.

One of the biggest problems for United this season has been a fragile defence and ex-Premier League striker Charlie Austin insists Pochettino ‘needs a whole new back-four’.

Austin believes Pochettino could look to sign someone like Rudiger, the Real Madrid and Germany centre-back who previously spent five years in England with Chelsea.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Manchester United need a whole new back-four,’ Austin told OLBG. ‘That’s first and foremost.

‘They need someone who’s going to be aggressive. They’ve got Lisandro Martinez, but unfortunately he’s injured at the moment.

‘The problem is that there isn’t just one player Manchester United needs. They’re in a sorry state of affairs at the moment. They need a whole new back-four.

‘Their back-four is exactly the same as the one they had when they got beaten 7-0 by Liverpool. So that’s your starting point?

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘I wouldn’t be surprised if Pochettino went for someone like Antonio Rudiger. Someone of that ilk: experienced, knows the Premier League, still mobile and still athletic. That’s where I think they should be looking.

‘Then you can build the defence around someone like that and bring in younger players.’

Austin also wondered whether Pochettino could target his former Chelsea player Cole Palmer after taking over at Manchester United.

Palmer enjoyed playing under Pochettino and was tentatively linked with a move to Old Trafford last summer amid reports he was not completely settled at Stamford Bridge.

‘Cole Palmer was phenomenal under Pochettino,’ Austin added. ‘He was unbelievable when he first came to Chelsea.

‘I wouldn’t put it past Pochettino. Chelsea and Manchester United do seem to have a strange relationship in the transfer market.’

If appointed, Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils will likely be a daunting trip to Anfield to face Liverpool immediately after the international break.

#1942. Man Utd interested in £75m Chelsea star ahead of January transfer window

Manchester United are reportedly weighing up an ambitious bid for out-of-favour Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto.

There were high hopes for Gusto when Chelsea signed the then 19-year-old for a fee of £30.7million from Lyon back in January 2023, when Graham Potter was in charge.

Gusto, now 23, has gone on to make a total of 144 appearances in all competitions for the Blues while helping the club win the Europa Conference League and the Club World Cup.

However, for the most part, Gusto has been forced to compete for minutes with Reece James when the Chelsea captain has been fit, meaning he has often struggled to get a consistent run of games under his belt.

James’ latest injury, likely to keep the Englishman sidelined until the New Year, had appeared to have opened the door for Gusto to nail down regular playing time under new head coach Xabi Alonso.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Gusto has not started a match in the Premier League since as far back as September, though, with Josh Acheampong seemingly overtaking the France international in the pecking order at Stamford Bridge.

Widespread reports earlier this week indicated Gusto was ‘assessing his options’ and ‘open’ to the prospect of leaving Chelsea in search of a fresh challenge elsewhere.

According to talkSPORT, this has put both Manchester clubs on red alert, with United and City said to be ‘interested’ and ‘keeping tabs’ on the situation should an opportunity arise.

It’s claimed it may take an offer in the region of £75million to convince Chelsea to part with Gusto.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

It remains to be seen if either United or City will make a formal approach to prise the former Lyon man away from west London this winter.

City’s rumoured pursuit of Gusto stretches back for some time, with Enzo Maresca understood to have been keen on a reunion with the full-back when he took over the reins at the Etihad in the summer.

Gusto has three-and-a-half years remaining on his current contract with Chelsea.

There are, of course, complications for both United and City when it comes to potential transfer dealings this January, with the former reportedly on the verge of a managerial change and the latter still yet to learn their punishment for Premier League rule breaches.

Gusto filled in as a makeshift midfielder during Moises Caicedo’s absence from the team through injury and there were some suggestions the Frenchman could continue in the role under Alonso.

But speaking exclusively to Metro at the time, ex-Chelsea midfielder Gus Poyet insisted Gusto should look to earn Alonso’s trust by becoming the best possible right-back.

‘I do remember one of the most impressive decisions by a coach – Pep Guardiola at Bayern Munich, playing Lahm as a central midfielder,’ Poyet explained.

‘It was big news at the time, because he had the quality. Chelsea have been doing this with Reece James, because they understand it’s a possibility. Now Gusto as well.

‘But any right-back becoming a good central midfielder? No chance. Because full-backs naturally get used to playing with the line next to them, either on their right side or their left. Nobody’s coming at them from that side, because you’ve got the line.

‘Now, when you play in the middle, players come at you from everywhere, and not every player is the same. So yes, for one game [they can play there]. Yes, for twenty minutes. Not constantly. And now we see Chelsea playing a right-back as a central midfielder every game.

‘This is Chelsea — we’re not talking about a fourth-division club with no possibility of bringing in a player. So yes, it’s a little bit strange. And I don’t think it’s ideal.’

#1941. Sheffield Wednesday suffer new injury blow as Dave Challinor learns more about what he has in reserve

He needs to know what he has by way of depth too, as injuries continue to strike at Hillsborough, with Max Lowe the latest senior player to fall foul of one, ruled out for the next six weeks.

All that was up for grabs between the Owls and Accrington Stanley on Tuesday was which team would have a home tie in the last-32 as group winners, and it was the League Two side who took it with a 4-0 win.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Wednesday used the opportunity to protect senior players, having a debut to Louis Poland and substitute James Kay, plus a first start to Denny Oliver.

It showed in a disjointed performance in only Challinor's second game in charge, the first being Sunday's FA Cup exit at the hands of League Two Oldham Athletic.

"I suppose it's what I expected really, the one thing it has done it means I've seen pretty much every player over the time I've been at the club in terms of first-team fixtures, youth-team fixtures, and a mixture today," he said. "But understanding of where priorities were and what was most important.

"Some young players have made their debuts and it was a really proud moment for them and things that they'll remember.

"Obviously the challenges which there's going to be but for all of them they should be better for the experience whether it's good or bad and should stand them in good stead hopefully moving forward on the start of their journeys."

With only 5,472 in attendance at Hillsborough on a cold night and no real jeopardy, the match was played in a subdued atmosphere.

"It's tough because it almost becomes like a pre-season game really where you're expecting there to be little cohesion because you're chucking a group together that don't train together on separate sites, put together really last minute in terms of what it looked like," said Challinor. "It was probably making decisions on some players even within the group we've got whether they're able and some injuries.

"We had to make structured substitutions so I went into it not expecting loads, understanding what it would look like and probably you have to get yourself in that headspace as early as possible so as not to become frustrated because young players especially are going to make mistakes. Some of the more senior ones in terms of minutes and football are still very young and still make mistakes.

"That was probably what the game looked like from our perspective. To run through a few that may or may not be on the fringes of the first team."

One big plus for George Brown was his first appearance of an injury-hit 2026, leading the line before making way at half-time.

"It was a tough comeback for him because an experienced centre-half who's been round the block and we played pretty direct into him."We told Connal (Trueman, the goalkeeper) if it was on to play, play, but can we play over, especially for the young lads early on and try and get them a feel. George had a right fight on his hands but he's got through 45 minutes which is brilliant."

Former Sheffield United defender Lowe suffered another hamstring injury in Sunday’s defeat at Oldham.

"Max has got a recurrence of the injury he had earlier in the season, so he's going to be out for a period, probably maybe four to six weeks," confirmed Challinor. “It’s disappointing because you saw the impact and the profile of him in terms of what we want to try and do in possession.

"That's disappointing for everybody, but something that we'll have to deal with.”

Sean Fusire captained the side from right wing-back, but will miss Saturday's League One game at home to Plymouth Argyle on international duty with Zimbabwe.

"He hasn't got the vaccinations to go to Equatorial Guinea," where Zimbabwe play on Thursday. "The plan is I think he travels tomorrow (Thursday) for the game on Sunday (the reverse fixture in the African Cup of Nations qualifiers), and Kieran (Morrison) and Jordi (Liongola) are away as well."

#1940. Man Utd sack Michael Carrick and provide update on Mauricio Pochettino arrival

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Manchester United have sacked Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed their new head coach.

Carrick led training at Carrington this week despite it becoming clear a change was imminent as early as Monday evening.

He arrived at United’s training base at Carrington just before 8am on Thursday morning, leaving less than two-and-a-half hours later having been relieved of his duties.

Behind the scenes, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox have sought approval from minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to part ways with Carrick, with a deal for Pochettino, currently serving as the USA men’s head coach, in place.

Carrick has been on the brink at various stages this season with United sat in the relegation zone in 18th place after 10 games, winning just once against newly promoted Ipswich Town.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

United opted against making a change during the international break in September and October when Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were the leading contenders for the job.

Carrick gave himself a lifeline as United came from behind to beat Roma in the Champions League at the start of the month. United also fought back twice from 2-1 down in the same game against Aston Villa on Sunday to rescue a 4-4 draw but the decision was made the following day to part ways with the former midfielder.

His staff are also expected to leave, including former defender Jonny Evans who was pictured leaving Carrington with his belongings on Wednesday.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Carrick’s departure marks the third season in a row United have sacked a manager midway through the campaign.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino’s first game in charge is expected to be the visit to Liverpool on Sunday 22 November.

Carrick, who had a brief spell as interim boss in 2021, took the reins again in January following Ruben Amorim’s dismissal, securing hugely impressive wins over Manchester City and Arsenal in his opening two games.

They won 12 of their 17 games during the second-half of the 2025-26 season, securing third place and Champions League qualification with a game to spare. United picked up more points than champions Arsenal managed in the period from Carrick’s game in charge until the end of the campaign.

United clearly benefited from the lighter schedule in that run with just the Premier League to focus on. With European football back on the menu this season, reinforcements were needed.

United signed three new midfielders in the summer in Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba but missed out on their top targets Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes who joined Manchester City and Tottenham respectively.

The club also failed to sign another left-back and a striker – positions they were in desperate need of cover for. United are paying the price now with Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko injured.

Before the comeback victory over Roma, United’s only wins this season came at home to Ipswich and against Azerbaijan outfit Sabah. Following a particularly harrowing defeat to Como in the Champions League, club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly challenged the manager’s tactics with the skipper dropped for the subsequent game against Chelsea.

Following the 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth, Carrick was applauded off the pitch by supporters who instead turned their ire towards the players in a clear picture of where the frustration lies.

#1939. Several players needing bounce-back performances: The five key battles in Genoa vs. Milan

AC Milan will make the trip to the Stadio Luigi Ferraris to face a Genoa side in good recent form in a Sunday matinee.

For Milan, it is a familiar feeling of having to bounce back at the weekend after a midweek defeat. The Bournemouth loss was followed up by a win over Udinese, then the collapse against Bologna preceded the derby win.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent setback against Ferencvaros on Thursday has left another bitter feeling, so now Ruben Amorim must galvanise his team again. It will not be an easy one by any stretch though, given Genoa have won four of their last five under Daniele De Rossi, and three in a row.

Speaking of needing a bounce-back, Adrien Rabiot was disappointing in the loss against the Hungarian side. Nonetheless, the Frenchman has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. Sergej Milinkovic-Savic was the last to get as many in the first nine Serie A games back in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Rabiot has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven). His opponent today will be Morten Frendrup, someone that Milan have been repeatedly linked with over the years. The Dane remains Genoa’s metronome in midfield, and the shield in front of the back three.

Summer signing Milutin Osmajić has been Genoa’s main threat in quite a low-scoring side, with four goals to his name in Serie A. He is keeping Lorenzo Colombo out of the side, though the Italian has provided a couple of assists for the Montenegrin when they have been fielded together in a front two.

After a disastrous performance against Ferencvaros, Koni De Winter will be hoping for a much better outing this afternoon. The Belgian has been in the headlines for rejecting a Belgium call-up meaning he will stay over the break, and he will aim to channel that same display against Marcus Thuram in the derby.

In addition to Rabiot, the other player to establish himself as a major threat for Milan is Diego Moreira. The Belgian has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for the Rossoneri, and that came after a bit of a slow start too. He was decisive in the derby, with two assists and a beautiful free-kick goal.

He is expected to have quite a free-ranging role on the right, but what will be very important is getting players around Goncalo Ramos to try and unlock the Portuguese. So, Moreira will likely come up against the left-sided centre-back Johan Vasquez, someone who has become a mainstay in the Genoa side having entered his fifth season there. He does have three bookings in his first nine games, so that could be something to target.

Speaking of Goncalo Ramos, the concerns about his scoring form (or lack thereof) are beginning to grow into full-blown panic. He still has only two Serie A goals to his name so far, one of which was a penalty, and his overall involvement in the Rossoneri’s attacking play seems to be fluctuating between very little and non-existent.

Amorim and the team must get him firing, or it will continue to look like €70m+ spent very badly. Today will not be an easy duel for the former PSG man either as he faces Leo Ostigard, someone who will be well up for the physical battle. As we have seen, Ramos can get frustrated when he faces players who man-mark him, so he will have to be smart and sharp with his movement, ideally getting some more service too.

With an honourable mention going to Christian Pulisic vs. Alessandro Marcandalli, we had to end by mentioning Stephan El Shaarawy. He scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for Milan, becoming a fan favourite during his time. The winger has also become the main creative force for the Grifone, having provided an assist in each of his last two league appearances.

Given his propensity to cut inside in order to create danger, both Mario Gila but especially Yunus Musah will have to watch the 34-year-old very closely indeed. Milan have been exposed in transition several times this season, and there is no doubt El Shaarawy would love to make a statement against his old club.

#1938. Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness

Chelsea are promising to be this season’s Premier League entertainers and yet manager Xabi Alonso seemingly believes less is more when it comes to possession.

Alonso has started with two wins from two league games in charge of Chelsea, with his team scoring seven goals and conceding five. So far, it has been a lot of fun – if not entirely convincing.

But perhaps the most significant numbers are around how much – or how little – Chelsea are having the ball. Having finished their 3-2 victory over Fulham with 38.11 per cent of possession, Chelsea had just 25.6 per cent in the 4-3 success over Brighton and Hove Albion and successfully completed 146 passes. Both were their lowest figures on record in the Premier League.

“The data is not important,” Alonso said. “It’s how you play and what we can do better. I don’t say ‘today we need to have 60 per cent or 20 per cent’. I never talk about those things. It’s about how to prepare, how to be more competitive.”

Chelsea’s third goal against Brighton, scored in the 32nd minute, best summed up the London club under Alonso to date. It took the home side three passes to go from the edge of their own penalty area to João Pedro scoring against his former club.

Jorrel Hato passed the ball to Morgan Rogers, he then released Hato down the left and the wing-back slid the ball across for João Pedro to finish. It was a devastating counter-attack and should have put Chelsea on course for a much easier win.

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

“After 30 minutes, we are 3-0 and probably, in that moment, we have played too much the result,” Alonso said. “It’s quite normal, it happens in many teams. I am sure in the future we can manage it better.”

It is one thing outscoring Fulham and a depleted Brighton team without having the ball, but can Chelsea do that against the bigger and better teams? We will get an early indicator in the next game against Arsenal at the Emirates.

Alonso’s approach has some similarities to the way in which Antonio Conte set up his Chelsea title-winning team. Just as Conte converted Victor Moses into an effective right wing-back, Alonso started Pedro Neto there on Sunday.

After Roméo Lavia had opened the scoring, it was Neto who grabbed Chelsea’s second goal against Brighton by drifting into the penalty area to finish from Rogers’s low cross.

"It's a nightmare for the goalkeeper!"Bart Verbruggen and Mats Wieffer's collision leads to Romeo Lavia scoring his first goal for Chelsea ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/q5awbdwVV0

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

But whereas Conte’s team gave up little at the back, Alonso’s Chelsea are yet to balance their effective transitional play with shutting out their opponents.

Neto was partly to blame for Brighton’s first goal, as he missed a challenge in the build-up to Malick Yalcouyé’s brilliant volley. Making his Chelsea debut, goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez could do nothing to stop it and can expect to be kept busy this season if things do not change.

“I have come here to challenge and to try and win the Premier League,” Martínez said. “I know the talent we have up front. I try to bring that solidity at the back.”

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

Conte’s Chelsea had N’Golo Kanté to mop up in midfield and that is an area of the pitch that is causing Alonso some difficulties. Manchester City target Enzo Fernández was once again left out of the squad and Moisés Caicedo was not deemed fit enough to start.

Caicedo was eventually thrown on when Chelsea were trying to stop Brighton completing a remarkable comeback, but he was quickly forced off again with an injury. The club have been exploring a move for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara and that need looks even more pressing now.

“We want the best for the team and that’s why we took a decision [on Fernández] against Luton and today,” Alonso said. “What’s going to develop? We’re not sure. We can prepare. We are preparing for all the scenarios. But I assure you that whatever happens, from Wednesday [when the transfer window is shut] we’ll have a good enough squad to compete in all the Premier League games.”

Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee had celebrated Lavia’s goal, which came partly as a result of a corner but owed more to a mistake from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen.

MacPhee, however, will not have liked Brighton’s second-half goals. It was from a short corner that the visitors managed to work the ball to Pascal Gross and his cross was diverted into his own net by João Pedro.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gross’s headed third goal also came at the end of a set-piece, but, fortunately for Chelsea, it was in the sixth minute of added time and Cole Palmer had already made the points safe for the home team before then.

Palmer had done little to impress watching England head coach Thomas Tuchel until he picked up the ball in the 74th minute, shrugged off two Brighton challenges and produced a brilliant finish to beat Verbruggen.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Fabian Hürzeler, the Brighton manager, said his team “dominated” the game, but acknowledged: “I think if you spend so much money on these kinds of players, like Rogers, Palmer or João [Pedro], then, of course, a team like Chelsea can rely on this individual quality. And they showed it in certain moments of the game.”

Palmer, João Pedro and Rogers are clearly going to be a huge problem for Chelsea’s opponents. But Alonso’s team cannot rely on having to score three or four goals to win games. And they might need to have a bit more of the ball.

"The game today was a special game for me." João Pedro says he was happy with his performance for Chelsea against Brighton 🔵 pic.twitter.com/fWSqWo7ert

6 - João Pedro today was the sixth player (and first for Chelsea) to score a goal, assist a goal, and score an own goal in the same Premier League game, and first since Tottenham Hotspur's Son Heung-min against Man City in December 2023.Eventful. pic.twitter.com/xRVjqkOY9D

The final game of the day comes from the north west as Manchester United host newly-promoted Ipswich. That game kicks off at 4.30pm and you can follow all the live action from that match right here.

Chelsea 4 Brighton 3 Leeds 1 Brentford 1 Sunderland 1 Fulham 0

Possession: Chelsea 26%-74% BrightonShots: 17-15Shots on target: 6-6Corners: 4-7Touches in opposition box: 29-28

There is no time for Brighton to push for the equaliser as the final whistle is blown at Stamford Bridge. Chelsea make it two wins from two to start the new Premier League season but were pushed all the way by Brighton. It finishes 4-3 at Stamford Bridge.

It could well be the last touch of the game but Brighton have a small amount of hope as Gross heads past Martinez. If that had come a few minutes ago, maybe Brighton could have pushed for a draw.

Brighton have a corner and if they are to have any chance of potentially rescuing a point, they have to score right now. De Cuyper’s inswinger is clipped into a dangerous area but for some odd reason referee Michael Oliver gives Chelsea a free-kick. Absolutely ridiculous decision; there was no foul in any way, shape or form.

Chelsea look to counter through Pedro, who is then brought down by Costinha. It is an easy booking for referee Michael Oliver to give.

How many added minutes will there be? The answer is five minutes.

Boscagli is booked for bringing down Rogers.

This is a concern for Chelsea as Caicedo, who came on as a second-half substitute, is now having to go off injured. In his place is former Brighton man Barco, who slapped Bellingham at the World Cup. Barco is booed vociferously by the travelling Brighton fans.

Meanwhile Leeds are level 1-1 against Brentford at Elland Road thanks to Calvert-Lewin’s equaliser.

Double change for Brighton as Costinha and David replace Wieffer and Kostoulas.

Brighton scored four a week ago against Aston Villa on the opening weekend but have conceded four this weekend. If they can get a goal though soon, it would make the home fans inside Stamford Bridge very nervous.

Kadioglu has an effort from the edge of the Chelsea box but drags his effort wide.

Meanwhile, up in the north east, Isidor has put Sunderland 1-0 up against Fulham at the Stadium of Light.

Palmer has been pretty quiet today but Chelsea’s two-goal lead is restored. He receives it from Pedro and drives forward through the Brighton half. As he approaches the edge of the penalty area, Palmer calmly slots home into the bottom corner.

Cole Palmer finishes EXPERTLY to give Chelsea their two-goal cushion back 💥 pic.twitter.com/6xI9W8xe2q

Tuchel will have like that. He may not have had a brilliant game, but Palmer just scored a brilliant goal. That should be enough for Chelsea.

Fabian Hurzeler turns to his bench for the first time today as Osman comes on for Yalcouye, who was impressive.

Xabi Alonso turns to his bench again as Chavarria replaces Colwill.

We have this news from the Premier League:

#CHEBHAMatch Officials are operating in the second half without communications packs due to an ongoing technical issue. VAR remains in operation via a back-up system using messages sent to the referee's watch and radio communication to the fourth official if required.

Dunk is in trouble. The ball is played forward by Gusto down the right channel to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Dunk brings Pedro down but is fortunate that Vuskovic was covering so that is why there is no red card. Dunk is rightly booked.

Chelsea are on the ropes at the moment and Brighton can sense another goal. Boscagli is the latest Brighton player to have an effort and Martinez is forced into a decent save down to his left.

Xabi Alonso is going to respond to the Brighton momentum with a triple change. James, Acheampong and Caicedo replace Neto, Lavia and Fofana.

It is all Brighton and Chelsea are seriously wobbling. Gomez has his fourth chance of the second half and is not far off scoring as his effort hits the side netting. You can sense the anxiety inside Stamford Bridge and it is the travelling Brighton fans making all the noise.

This game is well and truly back on. Chelsea looked in complete control at 3-0 up but now there is just one goal in it. Brighton work a corner short and appear to have wasted the chance but Yalcouye slides a wonderful pass into the right side of the box to pick out the run of Gross, whose shot/cross takes a big deflection off former Brighton man Pedro and goes past Martinez into the Chelsea net.

Joao Pedro puts Pascal Groß's cross into his own net and Brighton have brought it back to 3-2 👀 pic.twitter.com/maBMwVu3DC

Gomez has already missed two chances in this second half and he now has his third opportunity since the break. His powerful effort from the right side of the box forces Martinez into a decent save at his near post...

England head coach Thomas Tuchel is at Stamford Bridge today. He won’t have like Cole Palmer’s miss much and Palmer is probably the only Chelsea attacking player not to have impressed so far. There’s still time, though.

Chelsea have two big chances to score a fourth but cannot take either. First, Neto takes advantage of poor defending from Kadioglu and has a shot saved at the near post by Verbruggen. Then Palmer has a glorious opportunity inside the six-yard box from Rogers’ cross but somehow Palmer guides it over the bar. I am going to say it now that I do not think we have seen an end to the goals today.

Fofana is rightly booked for an earlier challenge on De Cuyper as he completely took him out and Brighton now have a free-kick deep into the Chelsea half after a foul by Neto.

Boscagli clips a lovely free-kick to the back post, where he perfectly picks out Gomez, who has a free header from the edge of the six-yard box but his powerful header goes wide of the far post. That should have been a goal and that is a mighty let-off for Chelsea.

Gomez has a decent chance for Brighton on the edge of the Chelsea penalty area but he fires his effort well wide.

Chelsea attack from back to front, with Martinez launching a long ball forward from inside his own box to pick out the run of Pedro into the Brighton half. Pedro ends up having a shot blocked inside the Brighton penalty area.

Palmer was very influential for Chelsea at Fulham on Monday night and, despite Chelsea scoring three first-half goals, he has been quiet today.

We are back under way at Stamford Bridge. Despite Chelsea being two goals ahead, it does not feel like Brighton are out of this one.

Chelsea 3 Brighton 1Leeds 0 Brentford 1Sunderland 0 Fulham 0

Chelsea go in 3-1 at half-time, having only had 29.3 per cent of possession. They finished with about 35 per cent possession in the 3-2 victory over Fulham, so it seems Alonso is setting his team up very much as a counter-attacking side. It’s all very Antonio Conte.

Vuskovic has a late effort in the first half from range and it goes just over Martinez’s bar.

The first half is then brought to an end not long after and Chelsea take a 3-1 lead into the break.

The Brighton fans enjoy an audacious Pedro backheel that does not come off. Moments later, Gross clips in a cross from the right that picks out Gomez in the box but his header goes over the bar.

There will be two added minutes at the end of this first half.

There has been a goal in one of the other 2pm kick-offs. At Elland Road, Brentford, who were one of the most impressive teams on the opening weekend, have taken the lead over Leeds through Schade.

After a dreadful clearance from Dunk, Rogers shoots from just outside the box but it goes wide of Verbruggen’s left post.

Pedro has a shot blocked inside the Brighton area before Rogers also has an effort blocked.

At 3-0 down, they looked down and out but maybe the visitors have a route back into the game. Kostoulas is denied by Martinez before the ball comes to Yalcouye, who volleys first time. His emphatic effort smashes off the inside of the far post and into the net. A fine way to score your first Premier League goal and maybe this game is not over quite yet.

"Yalcouye with a sumptuous volley!"Malick Yalcouye puts Brighton on the scoreboard with a venomous volley 😳 pic.twitter.com/8UeeyvPjUw

There have already been three goals in the first half at Stamford Bridge but it is still goalless at Elland Road and the Stadium of Light in the other two 2pm kick-offs.

The Brighton fans have been singing ‘The Falklands are ours’ at Chelsea’s Argentine substitute Valentin Barco. Barco was part of the Argentina squad who celebrated his nation’s World Cup win over England by displaying a Falklands banner. The Brighton fans had also been giving the club’s former striker Joao Pedro some stick. Pedro celebrated his goal right in front of them. Touche.

The Brazilian missed a sitter earlier but he makes no mistake this time and goes to celebrate in front of the travelling Brighton fans. Pedro owes a lot of gratitude from Hato, who drives down Chelsea’s left from inside his own half to the edge of the Brighton box. The Dutchman passes to his left to find Pedro, who takes one touch before clinically slotting home into the far corner. Is that game, set and match?

Joao Pedro finishes off a deadly Chelsea counter-attack and gives the Blues a 3-0 lead 🔥 pic.twitter.com/wAr0ckIgXJ

Brighton have their first real sighter on goal. Gomez clips in a lovely delivery to the far post to pick out the run of Yalcouye into the box. Yalcouye gets to it on the stretch and his effort is straight at Martinez.

Brighton have had 70% possession but their xG currently sits at 0.03. Despite having a lot of the ball, they really have not looked like scoring. You do though have to bear in mind that they are without forwards like Minteh, Rutter and Mitoma due to injury. Will Minteh still be a Brighton player when the window shuts?

How has Pedro missed? The former Brighton man absolutely should have put Chelsea 3-0 up and that could have been game, set and match. The ball is played in behind down the right channel and Neto outmuscles Kadioglu, who goes to ground near the byline. Neto then unselfishly from the right side of the box squares it for Pedro, who takes a few touches before getting his shot away. It seems harder to miss than to score but somehow puts his effort wide of the far post.

After Martinez easily catches a corner from Gross, the Chelsea fans start singing the name of their new goalkeeper.

Brighton are dominating posession but are yet to have a shot. Chelsea meanwhile have had three shots, all on target, and have scored twice.

The hosts have their second inside the opening quarter of an hour. Rogers does well on the left side of the box to hold off Vuskovic before squaring the ball. Neto runs across Kadioglu’s blindside and pokes home first time from eight yards out. Kadioglu should really have dealt with that and was too flat-footed. He should not have allowed Neto to get to that ball first.

"Pedro Neto Pounces!"Morgan Rogers goes past his defender before sliding the ball across to Neto! 💥 pic.twitter.com/WHZCIGsOLl

The travelling Brighton fans are making sure that Pedro knows what they think of their former player.

Up in the stands, England boss Thomas Tuchel is sat next to Brazil manager Carlo Ancelotti, both former Chelsea bosses.

Since the start of the 2024/25 season, no goalkeeper in the Premier League has made more errors leading to goals than Verbruggen’s 10. Second on that list; Sanchez, who is not in the Chelsea squad today.

Brighton win their first corner of the afternoon and Martinez is forced into action, punching away at his near post as the delivery threatened to creep in.

That is an absolute gift for the home side after a huge error from Brighton. Pedro flicks on at the near post and Wieffer makes the block near his own line. Verbruggen then tries to catch the loose ball but he and Wieffer end up getting into each others’ way. The ball then falls to Lavia, who pokes home. As they did at Craven Cottage the other night, Chelsea hit the front early.

There was a fist pump from Chelsea’s new set-piece coach Austin MacPhee after Romeo Lavia’s goal from the corner. It looks like MacPhee will be claiming credit for that one, even though it came thanks to an error from Brighton goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen. Xabi Alonso also celebrated with MacPhee.

Chelsea win the first corner of the afternoon after Dunk blocked Neto’s cross...

He might be trying to sell his shares in Chelsea, but co-owner Todd Boehly is at today’s game in the Stamford Bridge stands.

Before we get going, Stamford Bridge pays tribute to Bobby Tambling and Ken Bates, who both died over the summer. Wreaths are laid in their memory with their families carrying framed pictures of the two men.

Emiliano Martínez turns 34 on September 2 and by most tangible metrics, the goalkeeper is past his peak.

But it is the intangibles that set Martínez apart and why his availability at a knock-down price from Aston Villa convinced Chelsea to seize a market opportunity.

At £7.5m, Martínez could prove to be Chelsea’s smartest piece of business of the summer and there is little doubt he will be box-office at Stamford Bridge.

Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

#1937. Why Manchester United face a race against time to confirm Mauricio Pochettino appointment

Manchester United could be in a race against time to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new manager.

Carrick sack news LIVE: Man Utd latest as Pochettino accepts job offer

The first players Pochettino could sign as Man Utd manager

Ratcliffe and INEOS should be ashamed at how they are running Man Utd

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events

It has been widely reported that the former Chelsea and Tottenham boss is in line to become the next head coach at Old Trafford, with talks under way and personal terms close to being finalised.

Pochettino would replace Michael Carrick, who remains in post but is expected to be sacked following a meeting of the United hierarchy that is due to take place in Monaco on Wednesday.

It is understood that a final decision to dismiss Carrick has yet to be taken, but that CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are likely to recommend to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that a change is made in an attempt to halt United’s alarming run of form that has seen them win just one of their opening 10 Premier League matches and sit in the relegation zone heading into the November international break.

Pochettino has emerged as United’s No1 option to succeed Carrick, with the club understood to be willing to pay the $10million (£7.5m) release clause in his contract with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT), which was only extended until 2030 after this summer’s World Cup on home soil.

The Argentine has spoken to United on multiple occasions in the past and is known to be keen on the job, moving clear of the likes of Eddie Howe, Julian Nagelsmann and Antonio Conte in the race.

However, United will likely have to move quickly to get the agreement finalised, with the USA having an important two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie coming up.

They initially take on Haiti in Miami on Saturday, before playing the second fixture in Cincinnati next Wednesday. The USMNT close 2026 with a friendly against Jamaica in Fort Lauderdale on December 13.

The first leg against Haiti has been relocated from Kingston in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”, with Haiti having been unable to stage home matches in their own country since 2021.

Pochettino has been in charge of the USMNT since succeeding Gregg Berhalter in the aftermath of the 2024 Copa America tournament, finishing as a runner-up in last year’s Gold Cup and also leading the team to the last 16 of a World Cup co-hosted by the United States earlier this year.

The USMNT, United and Pochettino will surely all look to have the situation resolved before those games against Haiti, with struggling United returning from the international break with a huge game away against fierce rivals Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

Pochettino is due to address reporters on Friday ahead of the first leg against Haiti in a pre-match press conference, though the USA have cancelled media access scheduled for Wednesday in observance of Veterans Day.

#1936. Star of Mauricio Pochettino’s Spurs side reveals how he will change Man Utd

Former Tottenham star Toby Alderweireld says Mauricio Pochettino is the man to change the mentality at Manchester United and will bring intensity to the team.

Michael Carrick has been dismissed as Red Devils manager, with confirmation coming from the club on Thursday morning.

The club legend’s interim stint from January to the end of last season could scarcely have gone better, but his permanent spell in charge has been disastrous, with United winning just one of their 10 Premier League games this campaign.

Pochettino is now expected to be announced as Carrick’s replacement, with the USA manager set to leave his role and return to the Premier League where he has previously managed Chelsea, Southampton and Spurs.

His stint in charge of Tottenham was the most significant of his career, leading the club to a Champions League and second-place finish in the Premier League.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Alderweireld was a big part of that success, playing for Spurs from 2015-21, and he has high hopes for his former boss at Old Trafford.

‘He will make players fit, that’s for sure,’ the Belgian told talkSPORT. ‘Second of all he brings intensity. It’s not like everyone is playing their own game, he wants a team that’s going to be on the front foot. He wants to play pressure and having the ball as well.

‘A clear idea, intensity and players being fit, I think that’s the way he likes to work.’

Alderweireld reckons Pochettino is going to want the club to bend to his will to some extent, expecting the Argentine to insist on influence in the transfer market.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The summer, maybe the winter as well, the transfer window is going to be the players that he wants,’ said the former defender.

‘Also the facilities are going to be built also to the things that he wants. Making players fit, food-wise, gym-wise, everything needs to be how he wants it, that’s a big part of his philosophy.

‘Then he’ll want to buy the players. Maybe not always the biggest names, biggest talents, but guys with desire to win, desire to become better, desire to run. I think if you see the players he bought for Spurs, that’s thing number one, the desire to become better, the desire to win games, wins duels, to run.

‘That’s why I think Pochettino is the man for Man United, to change things around. In the past couple of transfer windows they’ve bought good players, good quality but they miss some chemistry, they miss the intensity and I think Pochettino will bring that.

‘He brings the mentality. If you work hard and bring your A game every single day, everything you want you can achieve. He will bring intensity and the mindset will change at Man United.’

#1935. League One attendance table: Sheffield Wednesday, Huddersfield Town, Bradford City, Barnsley FC & more ranked

League One attendance table with Sheffield Wednesday, Huddersfield Town, Bradford City, Barnsley, Doncaster Rovers and more compared

It is already shaping up to be an eventful season in League One - and plenty of fanbases are being tested.

Sheffield Wednesday have new owners and a new sense of purpose, yet have work to do if they are to bounce straight back into the Championship. The Owls, now led by Dave Challinor following the dismissal of Henrik Pedersen, sit ninth in the table.

Above them in seventh are Bradford City, who are finding their feet under Michael Duff after Graham Alexander’s abrupt move to Preston North End. Even higher are Martin Drury’s Huddersfield Town, flying high at the top of the three after just one defeat across 14 league games.

It has been a tough season so far for fans of Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley, who both sit in the bottom half. Grant McCann’s Rovers occupy 20th, while Daniel Stendel’s Reds are languishing in 23rd.

Different fanbases are having contrasting experiences but all remain loyal in support of their clubs. But how do League One clubs compare when it comes to average home attendance?

The good news for the Rossoneri is that they won the other two games in that run, and the five games before that were all wins as well, with no defeat recorded against the Grifone since 2020.

The most recent win was a 2-1 win at the Marassi in favour of Milan, courtesy of goals from Christopher Nkunku and Zachary Athekame. In the game at San Siro, Rafael Leao rescued a point in the dying minutes after Colombo had given Genoa the lead in the first half.

You can read our pre-match preview ahead of an important game before the international break, plus some insight on the resurgent opponents, while below are the best stats ahead of the game.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in their last 10 Serie A matches against Genoa (W6 D4). Since 2020-21, the Rossoneri only have a longer run of unbeaten games against Hellas Verona (12).

➤ Milan have won each of their last four Serie A away games against Genoa. Only against three teams do the Rossoneri currently have a longer running away win streak in the competition: Hellas Verona (seven), Messina (five) and Pisa (five).

➤ Genoa are on a three-game winning streak in Serie A. The last time the Rossoblu recorded a streak of four consecutive wins in a single season in the top flight was between March and April 2009.

➤ Genoa have won three of their first six home games this season (D1 L2). The Rossoblu haven’t won four of their first seven Serie A home games since the 2015-16 season, when Gian Piero Gasperini was in charge.

➤ Ruben Amorim’s Milan have scored 21 goals in their first 10 Serie A games this season. The last Rossoneri manager to do better after his first 11 league games was Cesare Maldini in 1972, with 25 goals.

➤ Milan have won two and drawn three of their first five away games this season. The Rossoneri have avoided defeat in their first six away games of the season on three occasions between 2020-21 and 2025-26, the same number as Inter and Napoli, and could now become the only team to do so four times in this span, including the current season.

➤ Genoa have scored four goals in the first 15 minutes of Serie A action this season, a figure they share with Frosinone, Atalanta, Lazio, and Roma and second only to Milan (five). However, the Rossoblu are the only team yet to score in the final 15 minutes of a match.

➤ Stephan El Shaarawy, who scored 21 goals in 83 league appearances for AC Milan, has provided an assist in each of his last two Serie A appearances. Should he also contribute to a goal in his next match, he would become, at 34 years and 12 days, the second-oldest player to achieve this feat in three consecutive games for Genoa since 2004-05, after Domenico Criscito in 2021 (34 years and 269 days).

➤ Adrien Rabiot has bagged five goals and three assists in his first eight league appearances this season. The last midfielder to do better in the first nine games of a Serie A season was Sergej Milinkovic-Savic in 2022-23, with 10 contributions (three goals and seven assists).

Furthermore, the Frenchman has been involved in a goal in each of his last five appearances, and the last Milan midfielder to do better in Serie A was Kaka in 2004 (seven).

➤ Diego Moreira has been directly involved in seven goals (four goals and three assists) in his first six Serie A appearances for AC Milan. Since 2004/05, no player has had more in his first six league games for the Rossoneri, equaling Mario Balotelli’s record (seven in 2013).

#1933. Gary Neville tells Mauricio Pochettino to reject Manchester United unless two signings are made

Gary Neville has told Mauricio Pochettino to reject the Manchester United job unless the club promise to sign two defenders in the January transfer window.

With United confirming the sacking of Michael Carrick on Thursday morning, Pochettino is now expected to take over at Old Trafford.

After Sunday’s 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa, United sit 18th in the Premier League table after 10 games, while they are also out of the Carabao Cup following a defeat to Brighton in September.

Pochettino, who has a $10 million (£7.44m) release clause in his contract with the United States Soccer Federation, has already reached an agreement with United over a move to Old Trafford.

However, Neville believes the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager should turn down United unless the club’s hierarchy can issue guarantees over spending in the next two transfer windows.

‘He’s going to be sat in the Anfield dugout a week on Sunday, do we think that this is an appointment that will take Manchester United back to a level whereby over three or five years he can keep his job and he can deliver what Klopp did at Liverpool or what Arteta did at Arsenal where there’s that gradual improvement, that feeling you’re on a journey where something can happen?

#1932. Huddersfield Town’s Drury’s freak injury as Radinio Balker calls for no more 3-week international breaks

As the Terriers only needed to avoid a big defeat to guarantee their place at the top of Group A, it was no great shock to see Drury watching from the stands but the reason he gave afterwards was a surprise.

"I've got two fractured ribs from shouting in training," revealed the head coach. “I've been told to try not to shout for a few days so I took a step back (on Tuesday) with full confidence that everything would be in the right place.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

"Jon (Stead) and Dale (Tonge) took the group and everyone's been excellent – as they have all season.

"And full credit to the players to respond from Saturday (when the highest-ranked team in the competition went out of the FA Cup to Exeter City), which was disappointing."

Tonge is an experienced coach, with spells at former clubs Barnsley and Rotherham United included on his CV, but has never been a manager. Former Towns striker Stead was co-manager with Drury when the pair took interim charge last spring, but became the assistant when the pair were kept on in the summer.

Drury will at least get some rest at the weekend, with Huddersfield's scheduled game at Wycombe Wanderers postponed due to international call-ups.

"I've just got to stop shouting," he said. "I'm going to try and get some pain relief injections over the next few weeks."

Meanwhile, defender Radinio Balker hopes this season's three-week international break will be the last of its kind, saying it is bad for players. This month reverts to the more normal two-week break.

Balker, who is in the Suriname squad for Thursday's friendly in Lithuania, came home early in the last break to play at Burton Albion, but still felt his time with his country caused the adductor injury he then picked up on his return.

"I wasn't away for the 16 days that my other team-mates had, but it was a long time," he commented. "You're gone from your normal situation where you have your routine and everything.

"I was only gone for eight days, or nine days, I think. To me, that sounds more realistic, because I came back and I think the injury I endured was probably because of all the travel and being away from my normal routine.

"I can only imagine that my team-mates had similar situations back in Suriname when they came back."

The break wreaked havoc with the League On fixture list, with games organised for both weekends, but postponed if clubs had three or more international call-ups. In the first weekend, that caused call-offs for all five Yorkshire teams in the division, who have had to find new dates for those fixtures.

"I would say two weeks or ten days is probably best," said Balker. "I did understand why they did it this year, because they just had the World Cup, of course.

"So I don't think they will do it more often than this, because there was a lot of complaining about it, but, yeah, the two weeks that is coming is probably better, for sure."

#1931. Mauricio Pochettino will ditch four Man Utd stars – the winners and losers under new boss

Mauricio Pochettino is poised to take the reins at Manchester United in the club’s latest attempt to reset the clock.

Having been regarded as a genuine candidate for the job at Old Trafford on three occasions in the past, the Argentine now gets his chance in Manchester where United’s situation is more dire than ever.

With Michael Carrick’s exit confirmed, Pochettino will inherit a squad that has been routinely booed off the pitch by a fanbase thoroughly disenchanted with a lack of effort on it. While there may be hopes of recruitment in the January transfer window, Pochettino will have to work with what he has at his disposal until then.

Metro looks across the United squad to identify whose prospects look brighter than ever with the new manager en route – and those who face the axe.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

With Benjamin Sesko starting just two matches this season before injury struck again, Bryan Mbeumo has spent most of the campaign operating up top. He could remain in that role until Sesko is fit again but both he and Matheus Cunha stand to benefit in their natural positions under the new regime.

Pochettino has favoured inverted wingers to help create overloads in the middle with Cunha in particular tailor made for that role.

Moussa Dembele evolved into one of the Premier League’s most dominant midfielders at Tottenham under Pochettino, carrying on the work started by Martin Jol at Fulham with the Belgian. Kobbie Mainoo lacks Dembele’s outstanding athleticism but his press resistance and running power with the ball will be regarded as key assets for Pochettino.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Mainoo does not have the constant high-energy output Pochettino has traditionally demanded of his midfielders but he has improved his engine over the last two years and his ability to break the lines could also see him play a key role.

Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick all lauded the qualities of Mason Mount despite injuries ensuring they never saw the best of him. Pochettino could be another to look favourably upon him if he can prove his fitness.

When in negotiations with Chelsea back in 2023, Pochettino was eager for the club to end a contract stand-off with the midfielder and was desperate to keep him and make him a key component of his rebuild west London. His own arrival came too late to revive negotiations however with Mount joining United that summer.

Mount’s work rate has never been in doubt and his abilities to run off the ball or intelligently drop into space could be vital. But with just one start in the Premier League this season, the same old doubts are in place.

In October, former United captain Gary Neville called time on the Mainoo-Youri Tielemans partnership, neither dynamic or athletic enough to last the course in the Premier League. There may only be one winner with the Belgian perhaps most at risk.

Tielemans is adept in keeping possession and progressing play but his lack of drive up the pitch is seemingly at odds with how Pochettino likes to set up his midfield. Pochettino was also said to have turned down the chance to sign the midfielder on at least one occasion after his name was put forward by the Tottenham board.

The same concerns for Tielemans could also apply for another summer recruit in Andrey Santos who looks to be another passive operator based on evidence to date.

The emphasis Pochettino puts on his full-backs has been huge during his time in the Premier League but it is the area of the pitch where United are perhaps at their weakest. Diogo Dalot’s shortcomings on the right continue to be exposed while a long-term replacement for Luke Shaw is well overdue.

Dalot’s prospects are brighter – while his final ball is consistently short of the required standard, his ability to get up and down the pitch will be important. Shaw can no longer offer that kind of service on the left and Pochettino may favour the energy of Patrick Dorgu.

Pochettino helped nurture Shaw at Southampton before his £27million move to Manchester in 2014 but the 31-year-old will now struggle to provide the intensity the role demands.

United’s defence has been an utter mess and with the exception of perhaps Leny Yoro, all should consider their futures uncertain. But at 34, Maguire is perhaps the most at risk.

Pochettino favours a high defensive line, requiring centre-halves with pace to live with it. Maguire will turn 34 in March and has been at the heart of a backline that has conceded 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Pochettino may favour the younger legs of Yoro and Ayden Heaven while Lisandro Martinez’s ability to build from the back could keep him in the picture for now.

Alan Shearer has hailed Arsenal summer signing Ezri Konsa as the early ‘player of the season’ in the Premier League.

The England defender won the Europa League at Villa Park but has bigger ambitions with reigning Premier League champions and Champions League finalists Arsenal.

Konsa has missed just one game for Arsenal so far this season, helping Mikel Arteta’s side open up a five-point gap at the top of the Premier League and enjoy an impressive start to their European campaign.

The 29-year-old was signed partly due to the absence of William Saliba, who returned from last summer’s World Cup with a serious back injury.

#1929. Harry Kane for England - the only non-negotiable in Thomas Tuchel's Three Lions squad

For really the first time in his international career, Jordan Pickford has genuine competition for his place as the first-choice goalkeeper, and Leeds United's James Trafford will be hoping for the chance to ramp it up with an appearance either at home to Croatia on Thursday, or in Spain on Sunday. One more cap seems likely, two feels like a push.

But his club-mate Dominic Calvert-Lewin just has to accept he was born at the wrong time – anyone who wants to be England's centre-forward in this era can forget about it unless their name happens to be Harry Edward Kane.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Tuchel has already confirmed the 33-year-old will be leading his team out at Wembley – anything else would be cruel.

Getting Kane to miss internationals is a tough job in itself. The number of dead rubbers or easy victories he has featured in is very high but no one should criticise him for being hungry to wear the Three Lions, or even to add to a prodigious goal tally which currently stands at 91.

Even putting him on the bench against the team he scored twice against in October's astonishing 7-0 away win with only a point needed to qualify for the quarter-finals would be an act of cruelty.

For starters: Thursday is the night Kane will be presented with the Ballon d'Or as the best player in Europe – and by extension the world – in the season just gone. It will also be the night he breaks Peter Shilton's record of 125 caps, a record he set in 1989 and extended over the next year.

Yes, internationals are more ten-a-penny than in Shilton's day with competitions like the Nations League springing up and FIFA's greed expanding World Cups beyond what is sensible.

But Wayne Rooney, David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Ashley Cole and Frank Lampard all made it to three figures this century without any going past a goalkeeper who might have played more often had he not been part of a Pickford/Trafford-style rotation with Ray Clemence early in his England career.

And to those of us of a certain age, 49 goals felt like the glass ceiling for England players.

Now it is hard to know where Kane will stop. A ton feels likely.

Bobby Charlton hit his 49th goal in his 101st appearance, in 1970, but could not bring up his half-century in five more caps.

Gary Lineker looked a cert for 50 at one stage, but got stuck in the mud when Graham Taylor foolishly lost faith with him in 1992, missing a penalty for 49 in what proved to be his final appearance, then being controversially substituted for Alan Smith in a European Championship defeat to hosts Sweden.

Alan Shearer only made it to 30 before his international career came to a premature end but when Michael Owen burst onto the scene as an 18-year-old, the record looked under threat again. His time with England fizzled out too, hamstring injuries cutting the country's last Ballon d'Or winner short at 89 caps and 40 goals by the age of 28.

Finally, in 2015, 29-year-old Rooney made it to 50 on the night Kane got his third goal. Thirteen more caps reaped just three more.

Kane has obliterated that, and looks a far more complete player than even then one who set a new record with his 54th goal in 2023.

Then he was a Tottenham Hotspur player, a brilliant No 9, but since moving to Bayern Munich he has developed into an exceptional "false nine" – spending as much time in midfield as up front, and even helping out defensively. He is one of the best midfielders around.

Kane was edging in that direction in his late 20s, but his time in Germany has taken him to a new level.

“I actually don't see a better player, but I see a player that believes he can win,” argued Gareth Southgate, the manager who took him to two European Championship finals and 98 caps. “That's happened to him in the last month alone would have given him another boost of confidence.

“If you sit there and you think: 'My peers, experts, the world has voted me as the best player in the world,' my goodness, how good is that going to make you feel when you've been a player that people said can't even make it as a professional?”

Like Rooney, Kane could extend his career by dropping deeper on the field, a chink of light for those centre-forwards, like Sheffield-born Calvert-Lewin craving a look-in.

His recently-signed new Bayern contract is due to keep him playing for almost three more years. At the rate he has been winning them lately, that would be 36 more caps.

The lessons of Lineker, Shearer, Owen and Rooney is that the end can come abruptly and unexpectedly. Despite what his hairline might have you believe, Charlton was only 32 when he retired.

Whether he makes it to 100 goals or not, Kane is a special talent England should be forever grateful for.

#1928. England confirm how Harry Kane's record-breaking appearance will be celebrated

The Football Association have confirmed how they will mark Harry Kane breaking the all-time England appearance record on Thursday.

Kane is set to start against Croatia in the Nations League and, in doing so, will make his 126th appearance and overtake Peter Shilton to become the most-capped men’s player in the history of the national team.

The England captain is to receive a special commemoration before the game, with Shilton to be involved, and the player will also present his Ballon d’Or trophy, won late last month in London.

Kane is already the nation’s all-time top scorer. He has scored 91 goals for England. The record was previously held by Wayne Rooney, who scored 53 goals for the Three Lions.

An FA statement on Wednesday afternoon read: “Harry Kane is set to be recognised as England men’s record appearance maker at Wembley Stadium on Thursday.

“The Three Lions captain is expected to play in the UEFA Nations League tie against Croatia which will take him to 126 appearances for his nation.

“A special pre-match presentation is planned to honour the historic milestone with current joint-record holder Peter Shilton to lead that activity.”

The statement continued: “Shilton has held the record since 1989 and finished his 20-year England career with 125 caps. The legendary goalkeeper is in line to formally mark Kane becoming the first Three Lions men’s player to reach 126 caps.

“Kane’s achievement in being crowned the world’s best player by winning the prestigious Ballon d’Or will also acknowledged on the night.”

#1927. GdS: Cisse and Jashari among six to draw Amorim’s wrath after Ferencvaros loss

Ruben Amorim was furious after AC Milan’s defeat to Ferencvaros on Thursday night, and some players drew his wrath more than others.

La Gazzetta dello Sport recall that Amorim deemed the performance to be ‘simply unacceptable’, a phrase he used in multiple post-match interviews. The concept was then reiterated in even more direct tones in the dressing room to the team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Beyond the words, Amorim wanted to understand, looking into the eyes of his players after the game, deeming them to be the reason for such a disappointing performance. Alphadjo Cisse, Ardon Jashari, Yunus Musah and the captain Adrien Rabiot are four specifically named.

The Portuguese pressed his players on why – after such an exhilarating victory as the derby – a display like that followed. As he explained post-match, the first topic the coach touched on was the approach.

From the opening minutes, the Rossoneri seemed at the mercy of the Hungarian’s pressing, incapable of finding solutions, ending the first half without a single shot on target. The team’s attitude wasn’t appreciated, nor that of some individuals.

Cisse, one of the key players in the start of the season and fresh from his first call-up to the national team, stood out only for his yellow card and was substituted at half-time, despite having played just a handful of minutes in the derby.

The Italian is barely 20 years old, and Amorim has already preemptively ‘pulled his ears’ to prevent him from getting too excited about his meteoric start. On Thursday, his substitution after 45 minutes said even more than the Portuguese coach’s post-match speech.

In the same boat as Cisse are Davide Bartesaghi, Filippo Terracciano, Jashari and Musah. Amorim is not necessarily pointing the finger exclusively at those who play less and started from the start against the Hungarians.

“The rotation has nothing to do with it,” the former Manchester United manager stated clearly in the press conference after the defeat. Also because, if the first half was a horror, the defeat was sealed in the second half when Mario Gila, Luka Modric, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic came on.

Now all eyes immediately turn to the away match in Genoa, the last match before the international break. The topic wasn’t touched upon during Amorim’s meeting with the team at San Siro, but it’s clear that the whole thing was a prelude to an immediate reaction at the Ferraris.

#1926. USA confirm cancellation as 'Mauricio Pochettino agrees to become Manchester United manager'

The United States have cancelled their media access day, amid reports of a verbal agreement between head coach Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United.

It has been widely reported that framework is in place for United to appoint Pochettino should current head coach Michael Carrick, as expected, be relieved of his duties, with the club sitting in the Premier League relegation zone on the back of their worst start to a season since 1986.

Pochettino is understood to be interested in the Old Trafford post, and according to The Athletic, his representatives spent Tuesday discussing personal terms with the club, with no major obstacles expected and a final agreement expected.

According to reports, there is a buyout clause in Pochettino’s USMT contract worth $10million (£7.44m) which Man Utd can trigger to bring back him to England.

The 54-year-old has not managed in the Premier League since a short spell with Chelsea during the 2023-24 season, though has previously teased a return to England.

“I miss the football scene in England. I love the country, its culture, the football culture,” he said in an interview with L’Equipe.

“For anyone with a competitive spirit who wants to measure themselves against others and test their limits, it's the ideal place. Here, you have to give your best constantly.”

If Pochettino is appointed by United within the next few days, his first game in charge will be against Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday.
