As for the game itself not good really. We got lucky to score from Genova mistakes and then got completely outplayed again by a weaker team. The back passing is so unwatchable. Even when they have space they just pass back running chances. Passing accuracy in general was bad.

A win nevertheless, the subs are just happening for the sake of it, luckily we didn’t end up drawing the match. Again I ask, could Barterzagi not have started this match and bring in Musa to rest Rabiot later on? The idea of playing players out of position by fielding the whole team strength is a long strech, I wonder how long we can keep it.

Musah didn’t “do well” because he was good. We were just lucky they didn’t exploit that flank and Diawara dill well to cover that side as well as pulling inwards often when the ball came from the left flank. Musah indeed had nervy moments but I guess it’s better than putting him in a spot where he has to be a full defender. He could sort of get away with it as an lwb. Ramos I’ll half leave alone today. After seeing the goals back again, I’ll say his movement did open up play especially on the first goal. I agree with the rater though that he should be taking that shot for the 2nd goal. Otherwise, he needs to improve his proficiency in front of goal. The usual suspects did well…. Cisse Rabiot Moriera. I think these guys are key to our performances once they’re playing together. Puli as well. The backline is coming along as well. It will take time but they’re a completely new one must remember. Finally, I can guarantee if it was our player who fouled an opposing player on the halfway line being what looks like the last man back we’d surely see red! This referee was atrocious. And then had the nerve to send off our coaching staff. Worse yet, VAR didn’t even bothered to take any look at all. This is quite bothersome. Rabiot would have been clear on goal.

I don’t know man, I feel like the back line is an adventure, every game. You don’t know which DeWinter shows up to play each game. You don’t know what guarantees you get out of Pavlo. Can’t expect a whole lot from Diawara as he needs to learn. Then Amorim brings in Terraciano… Good Grief. The only assurance you have is Gila.

I would argue that the back line can’t get reinforced soon enough…

Spot on. And then we’ve got a midfield overhaul on our hands as well, because Musah is bang average, Modric is 42, RLC is bang average and his contract is expiring, and Jashari is a bust. Can we afford such massive turnover, literally and figuratively this summer?

To add to both you and Vero’s points, our defence is quite “new” . These guys together haven’t played much together. It’s their first season as 3 at the back for the 3 of Gila, KDW and Pav (now Tomori, Diawara or other). I’d say give them some time and they seem to be the more likely of the area on the field to click. Because our midfield and attack seems more of a coin flip. I guess all three areas lol

You didn’t notice it, but Ramos on the first goal ran towards keeper to pull both defenders deep. This created that space for Cisse. Ramos 5.5 is insanity, he actually helped with both goals quite well

Don’t mind all these ones that their eyes are covered by his Price Tag and not his movements. You could clearly see he was point that Rabiot gives it to Cisse. If the othwr players were a bit more aware of what’s arount them, he probably would score more.. But we have players that on the final third most of the time, they usually only see the limelight.. He doea have his fault though which he is never in the box.. but that could be by design.

Ramos isn’t a midfielder, he’s supposed to be the 9, a central striker, the point man at the tip of the spear, the guy who’s #1 job is to SCORE, and #2 job is to hold up the ball. He should always be in the box! What’s worse is that when he does get the ball in the box, he’s too slow, clumsy, and lacking in ball skills, whatever, to get a really good shot off to score. He had a chance in the opening moments of the game and couldn’t get his feet set up to get off a decent shot! And THAT is why he passed to Pulisic rather than try to take another shot. He knew he was going to muff another really good chance on goal. Ramos plays like a midfielder who does almost nothing other than sort of fake pressing (when have you EVER seen him nick the ball off a opponent and start a key transition, like Pulisic did?), and then making all those “runs to pull away the defense”. That’s all the faint praise that anybody ever drum up to say about Ramos! Over and over and over again, those are the ONLY things people can ever say about him that’s good. Come on, you do NOT spend €74 million for a player to do stuff that ANY PLAYER can do on the pitch!!!

There are a lot of nuances, which you aren’t picking up on apparently.

Name me 5 instances of service that he received that he didn’t score from? i’m struggling to recall five all season. He feeds on scraps. He gets no decent service. He has to play as an AM just to help create something. And even though we didn’t bring him in to pull defenders for others to score, he is at least doing that.

You have to take his performances with a grain of salt.

Herean instance for you. Why did he pass it to Pulisic instead of shooting? A true striker buries that opportunity without even thinking. He is a PSG sub and a tap in merchant. I am sorry.

Spot on again. Lack of service is a Milan way of life. It’s probably because the supporting cast has always been hell bent on trying to score. Leao, Pulisic, and now Moreira, Hutchinson and Cisse are players who look to score first, not to assist.

I think in that specific instance, the extra pass was the right choice. He’s putting a man in a better position to score. In fact, I think Pulisic should have ideally let the ball run to Moreira, who would have had better angles with his left foot. Another example of Pulisic being laser focused on trying to score, as I mention above, and similar to his clash with Bartesaghi, but at least in this case you could say that Puli was in front of Moreira and thus did not really see him, as opposed to the Bartesaghi incided when Pulisic was behind him and should have deferred to Bartesaghi.

@VERO Who cares who scores as long as they are scoring? Ramos could’ve shot the ball there, most strikers would have, but he made the right play. Pulisic was in better position to score. Assist is just as good in that case. It shows a good team mentality. He could’ve been selfish, especially with all the noise he’s getting about not scoring goals but he still made the best play for the team. He should get credit for that. And this idea that Pulisic should’ve let the ball run to Moreira but is too “laser focused on goals is absolutely absurd. He was in the best position to score. Period. Not to mention he has no clue that Moreira is even running in behind him there.

You can’t win with with this site. If you don’t score people complain, if you score people complain that you are too “laser focused on goals.” People just love to complain.

Re-read my post. We’re saying the same thing vis-a-vis Ramos. I’m not one of the ones who is against him. I think maybe we overpaid, but as it stand I think he’s doing alright overall, and I think he’ll eventually start scoring.

As to Puli and Moreira, I’m nitpicking! Chill. Glad the ball ended up in the back of the net.

I guess this is going to be our status quo. Some good games or half good games, and some horrible ones (especially in the Europa League). Overall, I thought we started a bit poorly in the first 5 minutes or so, then completely took control of the game and scored to then stopping playing football by minute 30. I thought this is also a tale of 2 flanks, the right flank with Pulišić and Moreira & sometimes Gila stepping up was terrific while the left flank with Musah, Cissé é Diwarara looked a bit dodgy offensively. I don’t know what to think of this formula overall, but knowing Amorim, I won’t surprised if he tries yet another tactic with Ramos as an AM, Gila as a midfielder,… with him you can’t be sure. Maignan: Overall he was there when needed, and I don’t think he can be blamed for that shot from way out. Musah: I almost pity the guy. He started looking a bit decent in the midfield, then Amorim throws him as a RB for one game, then as a LB in the next. But I think it mostly shows how little confidence Amorim has in Bartesaghi & Estupiñán, which to be fair, is understandable. / Estupiñán: came in late and caused a foul that almost gave away a draw, such an Estupiñán thing to do… Diawara: Still a bit raw and rough around the edges, but overall I did like his efforts. Terracciano: we actually survived having him, Musah as LB then Estupiñán on the pitch… he wasn’t so bad this time apart from a horrible pass. Which makes me thing maybe against Bologna, we should REALLY have subbed him in instead of having Musah on the flank and weakening the midfield… but the past is the past. De Winter: I wasn’t actually super impressed by him. Almost gave away a goal one minute in and managed to make Vitinha look like Vitinha sometimes, but then again considering how much Gila steps up, I guess he can be a bit overloaded. Gila: I don’t like him leaving too much gap behind, but honestly his attacks look more polished than Pavlović’s. Moreira: not that good defensively, but offensively, my man is a demon. Modrić: Honestly, I think the recent adjustments of Amorim (or whatever one can call them), suit him a bit better. He looked more rejuvinated recently. Rabiot: some check if he has a knife, because he was tearing through Genoa’s midfield like butter. Cissé: his speed is a liability for sure, but this kid sure knows how to make himself available. Pulišić: his best game in a while IMO, he scored, pressed like there is no tomorrow, helped in the defense, won duels,… Ramos: the simple fact that in that position in that moment, he chose to set up Pulišić instead of trying to score himself from what was already a closed angle, is a positive. Overall, we’re 5 points from first place, which ain’t bad and I’m assuming inter is going to tear through Como as usual so we might be fourth. Let’s now hope the dreaded international break won’t claim any more victims from our side…

The more I rewatch these matches, the more I see players constantly staring at each other and pointing. Nobody has any idea where the others are going to be. In my head, this is about 70% ownership constantly turning over a significant portion of the squad every year and 30% management for constantly tinkering with the lineups so nobody can settle into a rhythm. Everyone get together and finally get things right to allow a little stability!

“which ain’t bad and I’m assuming inter is going to tear through Como as usual so we might be fourth.” Damn, I was hoping not to nail that one, but I unfortunately did.

Inter will walk to the Title. I expect ny January they will have 10 point lead already.

They will do so in spite of Chivu, from muscle memory on the back of what Inzaghi had built. But that won’t matter.

Don’t sleep on Roma. They’re looking very strong this year, and recently seem to be hitting stride. The title might not be decided until Inter-Roma on April 11.

I know we won, but taking our foot off the gas at minute 30 up only 2 shows the same problem as losing on Thursday. We don’t have the killing instinct.

60 min of Allegriball today makes me realize just how bad these injuries are. I can almost hear Amorim telling the guys to slow it down and conserve.

Look, Cisse is really good at taking his chances. That said his movement as part of the team is poor. I don’t see him as a 1v1 player. That said if he moves the ball quicker with his strong hold up play and learns to make the right runs he will be a very good player. What I did like about today was how the goals were scored by players working together. I’m tired of hero ball. ACM has no superstars, but they have some very good players and players with potential. I don’t think there was a motm, if there was it was Mike.

If it weren’t for the fact that Amorim pushed so hard to waste €74 million on him, it’s clear that Ramos should be benched and replaced by Cisse. Cisse’s natural talent for being in the right place at the right time and being able to get off really superb shots on goal, and to hold up the ball, qualify him as a natural 9, not a winger. As you said he lacks the speed and vision to pass to team mates to be a really good winger and playmaker. Amorim just can’t give up on the idea of benching his main guy Ramos for this young kid.

That’s a very limited observation. Cisse benefits from Ramos pulling defenders away and he doesn’t play where Ramos does, otherwise he’d get swallowed up by any decent CB. He benefits coming in from the flank, making late runs in and benefits from the defenders having been pulled out of position, like it happened today.

but yea, go ahead and play Cisse as a sole striker, see how it plays out.

We dont need $75M to make runs for others. His main job is to score. His “assist ” to Pulisic is a perfect example. It wasn’t a tap in for Pulisic and I actually thought he was going to miss it.

Instead Ramos could have hit the goal from you know…6 meters away. Easily. He is so bad that he couldn’t.

He’s just young and needs to know what he is going to do with the ball before he gets it. Yes, he has goals and his finishing has been top notched. But to really improve he has to see other players, understand what runs to make, and be faster on the ball. I am just reacting to some of the over the top evals. Let’s be clear, ACM has no superstars so let’s start looking at how they play together as a unit.

Let’s not forget we have a ton of players still injured and the subs really show that. Terracciano actually played pretty well but the rest just put the match at risk. Hutch can’t be worth 40 mil so he’ll be going back. Pervis… nothing needs to be said lol. Jashari is not looking like he’s the solution there. The rest of the team showed heart and grit so very happy with that. De Winter had one of his mountain top matches if only he could turn those peaks in to plateaus then we may not need to spend big on a “center” CB. Puli, Rabiot, Moreira, Cisse, just excellent as usual. Ramos… I’ve said what I need to say about him, not much has changed. This is not the role or team OR league for him. Really need the injured to come back and we can start to actually finish games comfortably. Great team win in a difficult atmosphere!

I will say that Ramos’s assist is appreciated and a striker with more confidence would shoot there 9 times out of 10. However, he barely got it off and Pulisic had to do a lot to make that a goal. I understand Amorim saying our play style needs to support Ramos more but if we’re talking about using Ramos as a garbage goal kind of striker where he’s playing mostly in the 6 yard box etc, then that may take years lol. In all the hold up play and everything else that goes into a good striker, I don’t see it. He wants to play slightly behind or off the shoulder of the defenders but to do that we would need to totally change our style of play. Right now he has to play in front of the defense and he just looks like a fish out of water in that area. Overall very happy with the team and Ramos shows a lot of heart but I still don’t think this is ultimately the place for him.

I am growing concerned about Ramos. No scores, 1 assist (today to CP). When will he begin to step up?

As usual, CP is targeted and on his butt over and over. Why do the refs allow this?

No scores is worrying but so are the turnovers that no one talked about.

I remember all summer long we were reading what was Amorim point percentage per game at United and how with the same team Carrick would have won the title if Amorim was fired earlier, don’t look now, but United might get relegated if they don’t fire Carrick. They are 19th on the table with only a better goal difference that keeps them from being last. Another great win by Milan. Keep stacking wins.

I honestly don’t put too much stock into what any coach does at Man U, Chelsea or Milan (sadly). Those clubs have all been run so poorly for an extended period of time that there is only so much a coach can do there.

Tbf Ramos participated well in the Cisse’s goal. He distracted two defenders and both of them followed him to nowhere and left Cisse alone lmao. But Ramos’s positioning still amazes me. It is like he doesn’t have any goal instincts. How is that guy a CF?

Well, the second defender was at fault there. Great move by Ramos but the defender behind actually sees that he was blocked by the first one. He could have stayed for Cisse. That was bad defending for sure.

Spot on. But now let’s just say Ramos has distracted the opponent defenders for Cisse to score. So then what? Who’s not able to run to the opposite end of where to score a goal yourself? This I get a smart striker occasionally does but this guy never does any other runs. This quality of creating space for others to score is one I’ll never get. The same was said about Leao too when nothing else was working for him.

Absolutely! I remember they were saying the same thing for Gimenez too. Literally the same thing..they were saying “he contributes, it is more than just goals” etc. And Ramos pass to Pulisic was terrible. He is lucky Pulisic didnt miss it. It shouldn’t even count as assist.

This is probably the last game to give Camarda an idea on what Amorim’s plans for him are. Up 2-0 he still couldn’t get anytime. He simply wants his $75M friend to score one. Desperate. Camarda should leave for his own good and career.

A few thoughts Positives 1. This was a really good win. We played an inform team in front of a loud crowd and came out swinging. There were some nerves with this one but a 2-1 win is a great result. 2. The Genoa goalie made no good saves. Mike made 3-4. He really is a world class guy 3. Ramos had a hand in both goals…he needs to score, but he was definitely a positive today 4. Cisse shows up in great spots and has a ton of confidence. Am I the only one who thinks he should be a striker? He has a poachers mentality, presses well and has good hold up play. He is not great in the build up or tracking back….so I’d love for him to get a few games up top. 5. Pulisic, Rabiot, and Modric….so smart and always moving into good positions without the ball. It helped keep that lead. Negatives 1. How long do we have to wait for Milan to be a team where most of the players have good vision? Musah, Cisse, Jashari, Hutchison, Moreira, Pavlović no one sees the pitch well. 2. Our depth sucks. As soon as the subs came on, our level of play fell apart. 3. If you are going to allow physical play, the ref cannot call that foul on Estupian. Such garbage

Amorim must know by now that rotating 5-6 players each match will lead to inconsistency and will ultimately get him fired. Today was a win with the right players on the pitch. And the right players in the stands.

From October 11th up until today, November 8th, Milan played 9 games in 28 days. Let that sink in before you try to complain about rotations. Also, outside of Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today. He has no choice but to rotate and use the same players because that’s all he has at his disposal because of injuries and lack of depth.

“Torriani and Bartesaghi all other players that played vs Ferencvaros played today.”

So that means he didnt rotate against Ferencvaros? Which is worse because that means he threw that game away by his horrible tactics.

He rotate the starters so they can get some rest. Did you watch the 2 games? What do tactics have to do if the other teams players play harder than Milan players? What does tactics have to do when Milan players pass to the wrong team, or cant make a simple pass forward? When Musah today lost the ball that led to a Genoa chance and Mike saved, was that due tactics or individual mistakes? At the end of the day, the players play on the pitch, not the coach. The coach can have the perfect tactics but if players make individual mistakes or fail to execute the tactics how is that poor tactics?

Important victory ✌️❤️🖤 Now the Germans are coming, so hopefully they will start cleaning the team of trash like El Stupido, Shіtshari, Camarda and always injured parasites like Loftus Merdus Chick, Chukweze and Salamaker!

If we are being honest, Milan’s two goals were ‘freak’ goals. On the first goal, Pulisic won the ball back on his own, then Ramos made a nice decoy run to open up space for Cisse. The second goal was a gift from Genoa. Milan’s offense created nothing the entire game.

Happy Ramos got an assist cuz he was vital to both goals, so often he makes the decoy run to open space for the 2nd runner. With better service he’d score plenty himself, but we dont create many good chances at all. Terra also did much better today, definitely crucial to keeping the 3 points.

I feel bad for Jashari cuz on their goal hes literally the ONLY one trying to close anyone down,everyone else just stands off and let’s him shoot… we really need someone who can create more clear cut chances for the forward line cuz we simply do not create enough clear cut opportunities, so many come down to the other side making an error themselves. Glad we scraped the 2 points out today at least

I hope in the next game Milan don’t rotate heavily….maybe 1 or 2 changes max. Otherwise next game it won’t be consistent again. You just have to stick with same players to gel up.

Milan exaggeration in playing in the back almost lost them the game. I dont understand why its so difficult for Milan in the last decade to build quick attacks. Nonetheless, 3 points earned. I hope the manager can fix these observations and realize the fans like a fierce Milan.

#1891. Arsenal injury update: Ezri Konsa, William Saliba, Bukayo Saka latest return dates

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal headed into the international break with a fresh injury concern over Declan Rice, after the midfielder was substituted in the win over Hull.

Those fears have since been allayed with Rice fit enough to join up with the England squad and he is expected to be in action against Croatia on Thursday night.

However, Ezri Konsa will play no part at Wembley Stadium, and there is some concerning news regarding the central defender - who has a fit-again William Saiba breathing down his neck for a starting place.

With that in mind, here is the latest Arsenal injury news and return dates…

Konsa has been managing his fitness after taking a hit to his knee during Arsenal’s 2-1 win away to Slavia Prague.

The defender was able to complete the full 90 minutes at home to Hull three days later, but Thomas Tuchel has confirmed that he will miss England’s Nations League clash at home to Croatia through injury.

“It’s my understanding at the moment that they will be both available but we will not take the risk. For tomorrow, both out for tomorrow,” Tuchel said in his pre-match press conference.

“You saw it, they were not in training. They follow their own programme, and the understanding and the hope and the belief, I would say, is that they’re both in individual training on Friday, team training on Saturday and match ready on Sunday.”

Should Konsa feature for England against Spain on Sunday, then he should be OK for Arsenal’s trip to St James’ Park to face Newcastle in their first game after the international break.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Newcastle (A)

It is just a matter of time before William Saliba is able to challenge Konsa and Gabriel for a place in the Arsenal defence after a delayed start to the season due to a long-term back injury that he exacerbated while on duty for France at the World Cup.

Saliba was able to avoid surgery, resumed full training before the Slavia Prague game and then travelled with the squad to the Czech Republic.

While Saliba was an unused substitute in Prague and was then left out completely against Hull, he was in action for the U21s the following day, playing 45 minutes of a 5-2 win over Aston Villa.

After being replaced at half-time, Arsenal’s U21s head coach David Horseman confirmed that was always the intention.

Arsenal given Konsa injury update after defender skips England training

Arsenal get new penalty review after controversial Liverpool decision

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

“He’s fine, by the way, it was all pre-planned, so nobody needs to panic,” Horseman said.

Saliba has not been selected in the France squad by Zinedine Zidane for the Nations League double-header against Italy and Turkey, giving him for time to work on his fitness during the international break.

Potential return date: Saturday November 21, vs Newcastle (A)

Bukayo Saka has now missed five Arsenal games in a row with a quad injury sustained after just 10 minutes against Bayern Munich last month.

He will also be sidelined for England’s Nations League double-header against Croatia and Spain during the international break.

Amid fears Saka could be out for action for up to eight weeks, Arteta confirmed that the winger’s recovery was going well ahead of the Hull fixture, but it will still be some weeks until he can make a full comeback.

”The way it happened, it wasn't a really aggressive action,” Arteta said before the 1-0 win over Hull.

“So that gives you some hope as well that the tissue will repair in a more efficient and faster way as well and he has some very good symptoms right now. So we have to wait and see."

#1890. Nottingham Forest transfer news: Oliver Glasner holds 'concrete interest' in Championship star

By Darren Plant | 10 Nov 2026 16:52

Nottingham Forest have reportedly identified Birmingham City defender Phil Neumann as a potential winter transfer target.

Oliver Glasner and his squad have entered the November international break with a 3-1 victory over Manchester City.

Having moved up to 16th place in the Premier League table, there is far more positivity at the City Ground than there would have been had they again failed to make the most of their chances in the final third.

However, Forest are likely to tinker with their squad at the start of 2027, particularly with plenty of funds still available from the sale of Elliot Anderson.

According to Sky Sport Deutschland, Neumann has been placed on Forest's shortlist of targets.

The report alleges that there is 'concrete interest' in the 29-year-old, who has helped Birmingham to the top of the Championship standings.

Neumann is part of a Blues backline that has conceded just 14 goals from their 15 games in the second tier of English football during 2026-27.

As well as starting all of those matches, Neumann has contributed two goals at the other end of the pitch.

While Birmingham are expected to shun any mid-season interest in the German, Fiorentina are also said to be monitoring the situation.

Neumann's contract at St Andrews is due to expire at the end of 2027-28.

Nevertheless, despite any interest from Forest highlighting his upward career trajectory, Forest already have a quartet of senior central defenders in Murillo, Nikola Milenkovic, Ousmane Diomande and Jair Cunha.

Realistically, Neumann is not going to be interested in going from first choice at Birmingham to fifth choice at Forest.

#1889. Where to watch Italy vs France: TV channel and live stream for Nations League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

France can secure top spot in Nations League Group A1 by winning away in Italy tonight.

Zinedine Zidane’s first games in charge of France have produced three wins and one draw - the only game where they dropped points coming at home to Italy in the reverse fixture last month when Michael Olise’s second half goal was cancelled out by Alessandro Bastoni.

Thanks to UEFA tiebreaker rules, France have not yet secured their spot in the next round, but a draw would be enough for them to advance to final eight.

Conversely, hosts Italy could guarantee a top-two spot with victory, alleviating some pressure on their last game - a trip to Brussels to face Belgium, who currently sit one point behind them in the table, ahead of their clash with Turkey which kicks off at the same time as this.

Marcus Thuram, who represents France but plies his trade in Italy for Inter Milan, has been ruled out of the contest with a hamstring injury. However, Kylian Mbappe is available for selection again after recovering from a tendon injury that forced him to miss three matches last month.

TV channel and live stream: Italy vs France is available to watch live via Amazon Prime Video’s pay-per-view service.

A pass to view the game costs £2.49, with coverage beginning at 7:35pm GMT before kick-off in Milan at 7:45pm (8:45pm local time).

#1888. He had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at 13, mixing with Zidane and Ronaldo. Now Jack Harper plays in Italy's Serie D... but he's not giving up on his Scotland dream

Published: 13:06 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 17:10 EST, 6 November 2026

Whatever the Italian word is for ‘steamie’, the steady migration of Scottish players to Serie A has been the talk of it.

The exploits of Scott McTominay and Billy Gilmour at Napoli have been comprehensively documented. Che Adams is thriving at Torino where he now shares a dressing room with Nathan Patterson. You can count Kieron Bowie, Josh Doig, Lennon Miller and Liam Henderson among the diaspora, too.

However, another Scot’s switch to Italy has largely flown under the radar. Back in July, Jack Harper, the former Real Madrid wonderkid and presumed saviour of Scottish football, signed a one-year deal with ASD Nuova Igea Virtus.

Currently playing in Serie D, the fourth tier of the Italian national league pyramid, the Sicilian part-timers were founded in 1946 and subsequently re-founded in 1964, 2011 and again in 2019. Which is to say they’ve had a complicated existence.

Harper can surely relate. Now 30, the Malaga-born frontman was 13 when he first made headlines, signing with Real Madrid after impressing in a youth football tournament. He spent almost six years with Los Blancos, learning his trade in its exalted ‘La Fabrica’ academy under the watchful eye of top coaches, Fernando Morientes and Zinedine Zidane amongst them.

If he wasn’t bumping into Cristiano Ronaldo in the swimming pool, he was having a blether with Gareth Bale or studying Luka Modric. All the while, he was quietly developing, establishing himself as one of the top scorers in multiple age groups within the academy.

Jack Harper now plies his trade in Italy's Serie D with Sicilian club ASD Nuova Igea Virtus

Soon after his 18th birthday, and with Real’s youth structure under review, he decided to swap Madrid for Brighton, signing a two-year deal with the then English Championship side. He couldn’t have known it at the time, but Harper’s move to the Amex Stadium was the start of a frustratingly nomadic decade.

A catalogue of injuries and bad luck kick-started a footballing odyssey that has taken in spells at Malaga, Getafe, Alcorcón, Cartagena and Villarreal, as well as Racing Santander, Hércules, Marbella, Linense and, more recently, Spanish fourth-division outfit Linares.

Harper joined the latter ahead of the 2025-26 season and made an encouraging start, scoring four goals in his first nine appearances before, once again, injury struck. He spent almost four months on the sidelines and, when the campaign ended, he found himself a free agent once more.

‘At that point, I decided to forget all about it until after the World Cup,’ he tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I said to my family I didn’t want to think about it. I needed to just disconnect.’

He and his brother Ryan travelled to Miami to take in Scotland’s final group match against Brazil and, standing shoulder to shoulder with the Tartan Army in the stands of the Hard Rock Stadium, he allowed himself to wonder what might have been.

‘It was definitely in the back of my mind that I could have been on the pitch because that’s the type of person I am,’ says Harper. ‘I know that if the road was a bit straighter and I’d had just a little more luck, then absolutely, I could have been there representing my country.

Harper had the world at his feet when he signed for Real Madrid at the tender age of 13

‘Years ago, I was knocking on the door when I was playing in Spain. I was called up to the 30-man squad several times but then the injuries started to hit and the door kind of closed. So yeah, of course I was at the stadium thinking I should have been playing. I know the level of football I’m capable of. I just never got a chance to show it.

‘But being there was a cool experience. The atmosphere was unbelievable and to see us taking on a Brazil side dressed in the yellow jerseys with those five stars on them, it was incredible. The World Cup’s the pinnacle of football. I was just glad to be part of it somehow.’

After that party in the US, Harper returned to Spain to discover he was a man in demand.

‘I had a few interesting offers on the table,’ he smiles. ‘I spoke with my partner and we agreed that, whilst our preference was to stay in Spain, it might be wise for us to consider all options. Last season was really hard and so we thought that maybe a change of scenery would do us all good.

‘Next thing I knew, I had an offer from a team in Iraq. There was an opportunity with a team in Thailand, too. That was very, very close to being done. But then an agent contacted me out of the blue with some deals from Italy. Soon enough, we were packing our bags and moving to Sicily.’

Despite the relative proximity of the two countries, Harper insists Spanish and Italian football could not be more different.

Harper rubbed shoulders with the game's leading lights in Spain, including Cristiano Ronaldo

Zinedine Zidane was just beginning his coaching career during Harper's time at the Bernabeu

‘It’s been a bit of a culture shock,’ he admits. ‘Football in Italy is much more physical. I don’t think I touched a ball for the first ten days of pre-season. It was all about getting fit and not worrying about the technical side of things.

‘It’s different, but that’s why I’m here. I needed to get out of my comfort zone. I feel like I’ve got it all to prove. Nobody really knows me here, I don’t know the language... it’s not easy.

‘But maybe that’s what I need. You know, thirty’s still young. I could have another decade-plus of playing in front of me. So, the plan is to get fit, stay fit and hopefully start climbing the leagues again. The hunger is still there.’

He adds: ‘I’ve kind of been on an opposite journey to a lot of people. I started at a huge club, maybe the biggest club in the world; I’ve had a good contract with a La Liga team; I’ve played in front of my hometown fans and heard them chanting my name. So, I know what it’s like to be there. It doesn’t scare me in the slightest. I’ve had a taste of it and I’m hungry for more.

‘Cristiano Ronaldo has shown how long it’s possible to stay at the top level. So, too, Karim Benzema. Even Harry Kane. What is he now, 33? And he’s just had the best year of his career, winning the Ballon d’Or. It’s not that long ago people were writing forwards off at that age. So, no, I’m still motivated and I don’t see any reason why, with a wee bit of luck, I can’t keep playing until I’m close to my forties.’

If Harper’s self-belief and resilience sound impressive, it’s because he’s had ample opportunity to work on them. In addition to his various injury issues, he’s had to contend with the weight of expectation that comes with being on the books of Real Madrid, intense scrutiny from a very young age, and, of course, plenty of rejection.

Harper moved to Brighton in 2015 but his career failed to take flight with the Seagulls

Perhaps the most memorable example of the latter came in 2015 when he was left out of the Scotland Under-19 squad by then-coach Ricky Sbragia. The former Sunderland boss triggered a backlash from former players, fans and pundits alike when he dismissed Harper as ‘a luxury player’ that his team couldn’t accommodate.

Spanish football journalist Graham Hunter described it as a ‘retrograde, almost prehistoric decision’. Harper’s dad, John, branded the description ‘harsh’, warning that Scotland could lose his son to the Spanish national team.

Sbragia subsequently apologised for his choice of words but Harper admits it took him some time to get over.

‘It was hard to deal with,’ he nods, ‘especially considering the love I have for Scotland. I might have been born in Spain, but I’ve got Scottish blood pumping through me. Honestly, the prospect of playing for Scotland was always more exciting to me than playing for Real Madrid. But that was just the mentality some people had at that time.

‘I was probably the most high-profile victim of that way of thinking but there would have been others as well, players who maybe weren’t as physical and so were written off. But I would definitely say times have changed. You can see that with more technical players like Billy Gilmour coming through and being successful.

‘The game has moved on from that kind of thinking and it’s a good thing, I think, for Scotland that it has.’

Harper, in action for Getafe, has played for a host of Spanish clubs and wanted a new challenge

Whilst his international experience amounts to a handful of age-grade caps, Harper has not yet given up on playing again for his country.

‘The beautiful thing about football is that things can change quickly, especially if you’re a striker. You only need a season or a season and a half of scoring goals, and your career can lift off again. There are so many examples of that, maybe now more than ever.

‘So, that’s the thing that keeps me motivated every day when I go to training. If I can get into a good rhythm, score goals and stay fit, then who knows what might happen? I still have that dream and that hunger to play for Scotland. That might seem a bit crazy to some people. Honestly, sometimes it even seems a bit crazy to me. But it’s the thing that drives me and it’ll continue to drive me either until it happens or I retire.’

Harper admits he would love to experience playing in Scotland before he hangs up his boots, having come close to doing so on multiple occasions in the past.

‘I’ve had phone calls where it’s been like, “Okay, it’s going to get done” and then, for one reason or another, it hasn’t happened,’ he says. ‘I came pretty close to joining St Johnstone one time, and Falkirk as well many years ago. The last couple of years, there’s been interest from some Championship sides. It’s a challenge I’m definitely up for and something I’d like to make happen.’

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 10 Nov 2026 16:57

Cameroon will look to strengthen their position at the top of Group G when they welcome Namibia to Japoma Stadium on Thursday for the third round of 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying.

The Indomitable Lions have collected four points from their opening two matches, leaving them one point clear of the Brave Warriors, who sit behind second-placed Comoros on head-to-head points.

Cameroon head into Thursday's contest in encouraging form, having avoided defeat in their last four outings, including a 3-1 victory over Comoros in their opening AFCON qualifier before playing out a 1-1 draw at Congo in the second round.

Those results were sandwiched between a 2-0 victory over China in March's FIFA Series and a 1-0 friendly win against Ivory Coast in Abidjan last month, where Bil Nsongo's 46th-minute strike proved decisive.

As such, Cameroon have lost just two of their 10 matches (W6, D2, L2) since David Pagou took charge in December 2025, after the Marc Brys-led side suffered World Cup playoff elimination at the hands of DR Congo, with one of their defeats under the current boss coming against hosts Morocco in the AFCON quarter-finals earlier this year.

The five-time African champions are bidding to reach the tournament proper for a 23rd time and a seventh consecutive edition, and they will be encouraged by their record of three wins in their last four competitive home matches.

The Indomitable Lions have scored exactly three goals in three of those four home fixtures, while keeping clean sheets in two, so they will hope to maintain that attacking threat against visitors who have struggled away from home.

Namibia have indeed lost each of their last seven matches across all competitions when not playing as the designated hosts, failing to score in their last six while conceding at least twice in five of those defeats.

That poor run has also been reflected in their current qualifying campaign, as the Brave Warriors failed to build on their opening-round victory over Congo at the Botswana National Stadium, their nominal home ground, before suffering a 1-0 defeat at Comoros on matchday two.

Collin Benjamin's side then endured an even more difficult evening in Russia, where they were beaten 6-0 in a friendly, meaning they have now lost seven of their last nine matches across all competitions, regardless of venue.

Nevertheless, collecting three points from their opening two qualifying fixtures does not appear the worst return for a nation that have reached the AFCON tournament proper just four times and missed the previous edition, though they did make a historic run to the round of 16 in 2023.

Cameroon and Namibia have been drawn together in each of the last three AFCON qualifying campaigns, with the Brave Warriors avoiding defeat in three of their four meetings (W1, D2), but their only defeat in that sequence came in a 1-0 loss at Japoma Stadium in September 2024.

#1884. How Harry Kane bucked every trend to become England's superstar

England’s greatest goalscorer makes yet more history tonight

Jose Mourinho once sat with Harry Kane in the manager’s office at Tottenham’s training ground and explained the difference between the two men.

Kane was a much younger 26-year-old then, the reigning World Cup Golden Boot winner but not considered truly world class outside of England. A prolific striker for club and country, nothing more.

“I have no doubt: you are a winner,” said Mourinho, on his second day in the Spurs job. He felt, though, that “the movie stars of football belong to other places”, that Kane was no superstar. In one of those rare moments when Mourinho brought the topic of conversation back to himself, he insisted that, by contrast, “my dimension is universal”.

“We have to build your status in that direction,” Mourinho said.

In the intervening six years, Kane has done so by himself, through dogged determination, constant refining of his craft, and the relentlessness that staying at the top of the sport for so long necessitates, not needing the help of Mourinho or anyone else.

Against Croatia tonight, Kane dons England colours for a record 126th time, 98 as captain, as he overtakes Peter Shilton’s tally. He will do so 17 days after beating Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to win the Ballon d’Or aged 33 years young, crowned the best footballer in the world.

He scored 73 goals for club and country last season, goalscoring of such mechanical, clockwork regularity it saw him surpass Cristiano Ronaldo’s best-ever campaign. Kane’s tally marked the second-greatest season of goalscoring in football’s modern history, trailing only the superhuman tally of 82 goals in 69 games posted by Lionel Messi in 2011-12. He had mentioned wanting to emulate Messi and Ronaldo in that 2019 heart-to-heart with Mourinho.

Yet stats have not always been kind to Kane. No matter the endless individual honours, the reminders of an empty trophy cabinet stalked him for years until his Bundesliga title win with Bayern last year. He is still awaiting a first Champions League title and a major trophy with England after two European Championship finals, two World Cup semi-finals and a quarter-final despite two major tournament Golden Boots.

The latter of those two Golden Boots, which he shared with five other players, arrived at Euro 2024, where he looked out of sorts while nursing a back injury and had to field straight-faced suggestions Gareth Southgate should drop him for Ollie Watkins. He stuck to the task and outscored everyone at the tournament anyway. He has 91 goals for England now, and this summer overtook Pelé for World Cup goals, scoring his 14 at a quicker rate of return than Messi and Ronaldo scored theirs.

Kane’s is a learnt talent ... four EFL loan spells toughened up one of football’s great late bloomers

And that has been Kane’s enduring quality: he delivers reliable results, England’s royal male. Kane was 33 years and 90 days old when he lifted the Ballon d’Or, fitting for a player who has only improved with age, whose nous and understanding of the game have combined with that unshakable self-belief to take him to heights not even he had envisioned.

He last week signed a new contract at Bayern Munich believed to make him Europe’s highest-paid player by base salary.

Kane is at his peak. As a player, first you are physically good, then you get older and have to get smarter because you can’t physically keep doing what your more efficient brain wants you to. Kane is in the cross-section — still a physical specimen but with that mature footballing IQ to boot. It is an irresistible sight to behold.

Comfortably the best player during his Tottenham years, where he became the club’s record goalscorer, the move to Bayern in 2023 has elevated him and made him better appreciated around the world.

Bayern’s honorary president, Uli Hoeness, declared him the greatest signing the club have ever made on the eve of May’s German Cup final. Kane then scored a hat-trick in a 3-0 win as they won the trophy for the first time in six years.

Bayern have come to appreciate the player Tottenham and England fans always knew they had — the striker whose tall frame and lack of searing pace disguise a Swiss Army Knife reality. For almost a decade, discussion has raged over whether Kane should drop deep as he does or should stay in the box. His sublime raking passes and deftly-weighted through-balls at a moment’s notice were enough to convince Mourinho, Southgate, Vincent Kompany and now Thomas Tuchel that Kane is best when he does as he pleases.

The romance of Kane’s story is that he is one of football’s sight-readers rather than playing his music by ear. His is a learnt talent, honed by repetition. Four EFL loan spells toughened up one of football’s great late bloomers.

That robotic repetition in training has made him a penalty specialist and a sumptuous ball-striker with an instinctive shooting ability, the ball immediately out of his feet and then driven, often low, precisely into the corner as though placed there by hand.

A 21-year-old Kane impressed in pre-season for Tottenham in 2014, yet Pochettino sat him down and informed him his body fat test result of 18 per cent was the highest in the team. Pochettino urged him to work harder: “You can be the best striker in the world.” Kane’s unwavering belief in that statement is, more than anything, what has propelled him there.

Anthony Gordon this summer gave the definitive assessment of what it is like to work with Walthamstow’s finest.

It is no accident. Every drill, he does it with seriousness. He never ever messes about

“Anyone at this level can put the ball in the top corner,” Gordon said. “It’s his consistency every single day in training and every game. He’s having a season that has only ever been beaten by the greatest footballer of all time; that speaks to the level he is playing at. You want to pick up as many habits and watch everything he does, to see why he is at that level.

“It is no accident. Every drill, he does it with seriousness. He never ever messes about.”

The complete player, he has spent the last 12 years representing Tottenham, Bayern and England and been the central cog in all three machines, never knowing anything other than being the man to whom others turn.

Some of his rivals for the Ballon d’Or had launched cringey PR campaigns when voting went live. In an answer to The Standard about this, he admitted in the lead up: “It’s just not my personality to talk about myself in that light.”

His body of work spoke for itself in the end. His acceptance speech featured motivation young children heading to Wembley on Thursday evening could do with hearing. “Anything is possible with hard work when no one else is watching.” Everyone is watching him now.

Ahead of another record-breaking night for England’s captain and leader by example, it is worth asking: has Kane proven Mourinho wrong? A movie star? Even now, not really his style. But by staying in his lane and grafting in silence, Kane has joined them — working his way up to the leading role, in his own, very English, way.

#1883. Italy vs. France: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Jonathan O'Shea | 10 Nov 2026 17:02, Last updated: 10 Nov 2026 17:05

Longstanding rivals, Italy and France have been crowned global champions six times between them, with several crucial clashes deciding which side would go on to collect silverware.

Most notably, they met in the 2006 World Cup final, which was decided on penalties after France talisman Zinedine Zidane saw red for his infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi. After one early goal apiece - including Zidane's pinpoint free kick - football's biggest game eventually went Italy's way.

Success marked revenge for the Azzurri, following their dramatic defeat to Les Bleus in the Euro 2000 decider. On that occasion, a late strike by Sylvain Wiltord sent the final into extra time, before David Trezeguet's 'golden goal' secured another trophy for the reigning world champions.

Looking further back, Italy were traditionally the dominant side - claiming 17 wins from the first 26 meetings - but France were ascendant from 1982 on.

Inspired by Juventus star Michel Platini, Les Bleus started to pick up regular victories, and they had gone nine games unbeaten against the Azzurri before that fateful night in June 2006.

The streak notably featured a penalty shootout triumph at the 1998 World Cup on home turf, which Zidane and co would ultimately go on to win.

More recently, the pair have played out three Nations League contests: in the 2024-25 campaign, either side won 3-1 away from home.

Then, in October 2026 - with Zidane now France boss - they settled for a 1-1 draw in Paris, where Alessandro Bastoni's strike cancelled out Michael Olise's opening goal.

Oct 02, 2026: France 1-1 Italy (UEFA Nations League)

Nov 17, 2024: Italy 1-3 France (UEFA Nations League)

Sep 06, 2024: France 1-3 Italy (UEFA Nations League)

Jun 01, 2018: France 3-1 Italy (International Friendlies)

Sep 01, 2016: Italy 1-3 France (International Friendlies)

Nov 14, 2012: Italy 1-2 France (International Friendlies)

Jun 17, 2008: Italy 2-0 France (European Championship)

Sep 08, 2007: Italy 0-0 (European Championship Qualifiers)

Sep 06, 2006: France 3-1 Italy (European Championship Qualifiers)

Jul 09, 2006: Italy 1-1 France (World Cup)

#1882. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

In this scrupulously detailed account of Arsenal’s summer, Sam Dean assesses where things went right, and wrong, for the Premier League champions in the transfer market.

They have buttressed the two areas in which they were already strong by signing Bruno Guimaraes and Ezri Konsa, but failed to sign the level-raising forward Mikel Arteta coveted.

In fact, with Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli departing (as well as Ethan Nwaneri moving on loan), their weakest department is arguably weaker than this time last year. Christos Tzolis, signed for £34m from Club Brugge, is their only attacking purchase.

But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.

I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.

To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.

Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.

This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.

You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.

I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

Jack Grealish to Everton is done. A small gathering of fans are waiting outside Finch Farm, the club’s training base, but the calmness of this little road, will be at odds with the scrambling that is going on behind closed doors.

Zirkzee is staying at United. No move to Everton. United want the cover in attack and Everton’s approach happened too late with no chance of replacing him.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move from Chelsea to Spurs has been confirmed.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

The fee means Premier League spending has now surpassed the previous record for a summer window which stood at £3.14bn. The running tally now stands at £3.193bn.

Ndiaye says: “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up.

“To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands.

“It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good.

“I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit.

“City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.”

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea have set Manchester City a £120m asking price for the Argentina midfielder. Here’s a look at Fernandez’s career numbers...

With Woltemade travelling to undergo a medical with Juventus for a loan move from Newcastle, that would appear to shut off one potential exit route for Joshua Zirkzee. Juventus had been looking at a season long loan for Zirkzee. Fiorentina have also been keen on Zirkzee and made an offer to United of a loan plus €30m (£25.7m) buy option but the Netherlands forward turned down the chance to go there. United would be more likely to bring in another player, probably a left-back rather than a direct replacement, if Zirkzee was to go but time running out on that front.

United had hoped to sell Manuel Ugarte and Zirkzee this summer and were in the market for buyers for Marcus Rashford, but the window could close with all three staying put. Ugarte’s serious knee injury put paid to the Uruguay midfielder leaving and Rashford has been reintergrated in the squad after Barcelona opted against taking up an option to sign him permanently.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. The Portuguese midfielder has never cut it in the Premier League and it is no surprise that Arsenal have cashed in. They paid more than £30m to sign him from Porto in 2022 but he has never come close to justifying the fee. In truth, it’s one of their worst transfers under Mikel Arteta.

Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Announcing Ansah! ✍️🔗 https://t.co/gweqxOt7aR pic.twitter.com/geZR60ZaTG

The Argentina forward missed three training sessions last week and was not included in Diego Simeone’s squad that travelled to Sevilla last weekend.

Nueva sesión de trabajo del Atleti en Majadahonda esta mañana. Julián Alvarez entrenando con normalidad con el resto del grupo. Objetivo, intentar estar en la lista de convocados para el partido ante el Athletic. Sorloth será baja por lesión. Imagen: @jsancris_ #ClubUria pic.twitter.com/IXAWX7mwrJ

Plenty of chatter about the future of Roma midfielder Manu Koné, who is linked with a move to Chelsea. The France international would be a strong acquisition for Xabi Alonso, but could his potential signing precede an Enzo Fernández exit? All will be revealed in due course...

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.
