#1824. Three outside contenders who could replace Michael Carrick as Man United's next manager

By Ben Sully | 10 Nov 2026 23:44, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:47

Manchester United are said to be on the brink of parting ways with head coach Michael Carrick, with the team languishing in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their 10 matches.

While a final decision is yet to be confirmed, rumours are already swirling about who the club could pick as Carrick's replacement should they decide to change head coach over the international break.

USA boss Mauricio Pochettino is reportedly towards the top of the club's managerial shortlist, with his current contract believed to contain a release clause.

Meanwhile, the Red Devils have also been linked with former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe, ex-Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann and the vastly experienced Antonio Conte, who previously managed Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur in the Premier League.

While the aforementioned quartet are believed to be among the main contenders, there may be alternative candidates who are at least on Man United's radar.

With that in mind, Sports Mole highlights three outside picks the Red Devils could consider if they decide to replace Carrick.

According to the latest odds, Kieran McKenna is among the potential contenders for the Man United job, although he is seen as an outsider compared to the likes of Pochettino, Howe, Nagelsmann and Conte.

There is a temptation to say that McKenna ‘knows the club’, but instead of using that tired old cliche, it is perhaps better to say he is someone who will be well-known by many figures at the club, and with that, there is less uncertainty about the way he works as a coach.

McKenna spent a couple of years working as the Under-18 coach at Man United before he was promoted to the role of assistant manager, where he worked with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, Jose Mourinho, Ralf Rangnick and Carrick.

The 40-year-old ultimately decided to forge his own path as a manager when he took the top job at Ipswich Town in December 2021, going on to lead the club to back-to-back promotions before suffering Premier League relegation in the 2024-25 campaign.

Ipswich stuck with McKenna and were rewarded with another promotion-winning season, but he ultimately decided against overseeing the club’s latest Premier League campaign, instead opting to take a break from football management.

Considering it has been five months since he made that decision, it is unclear whether McKenna is now ready to jump back into the game, although the chance to manage a club of Man United’s stature would surely be a convincing factor.

There may be a tendency to think he would be a similar appointment to Solskjaer and Carrick due to his previous connections with the club, but he has already built a stronger CV than the aforementioned pair, and his willingness to use width as a means of attack would suit a philosophy that has previously been associated with Man United.

With Fabian Hurzeler and Marco Rose currently impressing at Brighton & Hove Albion and Bournemouth, Man United may want to look to Bundesliga’s exciting coaching talent for their next boss.

Stuttgart boss Sebastian Hoeness is seen as one of the league’s best coaches, even though his side has struggled for consistency this season.

Hoeness got his first taste as a Bundesliga head coach at Hoffenheim, where he oversaw 11th and ninth-placed finishes before taking a year out of management.

In April 2023, the 44-year-old got the call from Stuttgart, who were languishing at the bottom of the table at the time of his appointment.

Hoeness lifted the club out of the automatic relegation spots before he guided them to victory in the relegation/promotion playoff against Hamburg.

Stuttgart’s transformation under Hoeness was there for all to see when the club achieved a runners-up finish in 2023-24, their best league finish in 17 years.

While there was a drop-off in the next Bundesliga campaign, any frustration from a ninth-placed finish was made to feel insignificant by Stuttgart’s triumphant DFB-Pokal, which ended the club’s 28-year wait for glory in the domestic cup.

Champions League qualification followed in the 2025-26 campaign, an achievement that means Hoeness is yet to experience an unsuccessful season at Stuttgart, the sort of consistency that Man United could certainly benefit from.

Hoeness has shown a willingness throughout his coaching career to select a formation that best suits the player profiles in his squad, while still having a clear philosophy to certain aspects of the game, including the willingness for his teams to push full-backs and wing-backs high in a bid to get in good crossing positions.

Out of the three options, Marcelino is the biggest curveball on this list, although he has much more senior management experience than McKenna and Hoeness.

While he may be relatively unknown to an English audience, he has a strong reputation in Spain as a wily operator who tends to command the respect of his players.

Marcelino has managed some of Spain’s biggest clubs, including Sevilla, Valencia and Athletic Club.

The 61-year-old guided Valencia to their first Copa del Rey triumph in 11 years in the 2018-19 season, while he beat Real Madrid for the Spanish Super Cup during his time in charge of Athletic.

However, he perhaps spent his best years in charge of Villarreal, first for a spell from 2013 to 2016 before spending three more years in charge from 2023 to 2026.

In his first stint in charge, Marcelino guided the Yellow Submarine to promotion before achieving three consecutive top-three finishes in La Liga and a run to the Europa League semi-finals in 2015-16.

After returning to the club in November 2023, the experienced coach steered the club to an eighth-placed finish, before leading them to Champions League qualification in back-to-back seasons.

In fact, he guided the club to third spot last season, their best top-flight placing since finishing runners-up in 2007-08, but it proved to be his final campaign in charge after failing to agree terms on a new contract.

Inigo Perez’s struggle to find consistency since taking over the reins at Villarreal has only added to the sense that the club may have made a mistake by allowing him to depart.

However, Villarreal’s potential error may be an opportunity for another club, and while it would be a left-field decision to choose him as Carrick’s replacement, he possesses over 800 games of senior managerial experience, has already coached clubs with demanding fanbases and would not be fazed by the Red Devils’ precarious position in the Premier League relegation zone.

His pragmatism has sometimes been used against him as a criticism, but it may be just what Man United need after shipping 19 goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Marcelino's keenness to play quickly through the lines and hit teams on the counter may also suit a team that is struggling for confidence in midfield and has players in advanced areas who can race in behind defences.

#1823. VAR a scourge on the Premier League as Forest denied by off-field meddling

Almost £3.5bn was splurged on transfers this summer in a league supposedly described as the best in the world, so why does VAR continue to prove so ineffective and divisive?

Seven years after its introduction, it remains a scourge on the Premier League and here at the City Ground was another exhibit of maddening off-field meddling.

Tottenham Hotspur avoided a third successive defeat after the crucial intervention of VAR prevented Neco Williams from securing Oliver Glasner his first win as Nottingham Forest’s head coach.

The big moment occurred in the 65th minute. Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goal-line.

Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot. The VAR review ruled that Williams had handled the ball, yet in this billion-pound industry there was not one camera angle which proved entirely conclusive.

On this occasion the VAR official was Peter Bankes, recommending to referee Craig Pawson that the goal be disallowed. Williams said: “It’s a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I’ve seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it because I never did. I headed it in between my arms. I’m at a loss at that one, it’s disappointing. If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t hit my arm.”

Glasner and the other Forest players were also incensed, and once again supporters are questioning how critical moments in matches are being decided by officials sitting at Stockley Park. “I think the VAR can’t intervene when he is guessing,” said Glasner. “I told the referee after the game that I felt the goal should have stood.

“The VAR should say to stay with the onfield decision because it is about strengthening the referee. If it’s not 100 per cent clear, stick to the onfield decision.  We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention this year should be very high which is why this is wrong.”

While Tottenham were perhaps fortunate to pick up their first point, they are still waiting to score their first Premier League goal of the season. They did not manage a shot on target.

The grand £350m rebuild is proving a slow-burner and it is only Mykhailo Mudryk who will have cause to remember such a dull affair. Signed on loan from Chelsea on deadline day, Mudryk made his first appearance since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

The Ukrainian forward was introduced with 16 minutes left, with his manager Roberto De Zerbi determined to reinvigorate his career.

Tottenham are still waiting for lift-off but De Zerbi remains convinced that his team will eventually click, particularly in attacking areas.

One of their summer arrivals, Omar Marmoush, wasted their best chance in the 16th minute by drilling a shot wide of the post. De Zerbi said: “In the last third we have to improve. We have to maybe keep more calm when we are very close to doing something important.

“If we improve in the last third I think we can score many goals because we have the players with big qualities. We could have scored three or four goals.

Considering we were only all working together on Thursday for the first time, this is the right spirit and the right way to move on.” On Mudryk, De Zerbi said: “He’s working to reach the best physical condition and he needs time.”

After the disallowed Williams goal, Forest were feeling further aggrieved soon after when Rodrigo Bentancur appeared to pull back substitute Igor Jesus in the penalty area. These are two teams clearly in period of transition and patience will be required from both sets of supporters.

It’s full time at GTech Stadium: Brentford 1 Sunderland 1

Pierre Sage has his first win while Alvaro Arbeloa has lost his first three Premier League games and go to Anfield next Saturday. Frank de Boer vibes.

City needed Donnarumma to spare their blushes with several good saves.

Brighton 1 Leeds 1. Pascal Gross missed a late sitter and Leeds are still winless in Brighton’s ‘new’ stadium in 11 visits.

It remains 0-0 so Spurs are goalless in three, both sides remain winless.

Iliman Ndiaye took a knock and has come off after treatment. He has sat on the bench, though, rather than headed down the tunnel, which suggests it is not an injury.

Enzo Le Fee equalises from the penalty spot.

VAR does not intervene after Lewis-Potter was penalised for holding. Le Fee chipped a pen straight at the keeper there last season.

Ellis Simms with the latest, clocking Donnarumma flush in the face with his close-range effort.

And it’s a third goal from a  left-back, but this time it’s the substitute Ben Chilwell.

Enzo jeered by Coventry fans when taken off was predictable. Replaced by Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Jaidon Anthony bundled the ball in but had used his hands.

And Mykhailo Mudryk is on for his first appearance since November 2024.

Forest are feeling aggrieved over that disallowed goal. Replays appeared to show the ball went in off Williams’ knee and he was protecting his face with his hands to avoid a stray boot.

Big cheer for Phil Foden when he came on for Rayan Cherki. Cherki has been creative for City and this might be trying another mode of attack for Enzo Maresca or saving legs for the Champions League in midweek. They have two full days of rest before facing Porto on Tuesday.

That is a big chance for Coventry. Loum Tchaouna got room in the penalty area and it needed Gianluigi Donnarumma to save low to his right.

Luka Vuskovic heads in from an inswinging corner.

Controversy at the City Ground – and it’s again a result of Var.

Morgan Gibbs-White’s chip over Antonin Kinsky should have been dealt with by Sandro Tonali and Jan Paul van Hecke but both players got themselves in a muddle and Neco Williams bundled the ball in from almost on the goalline.

The goal did go to Var for a possible handball by Williams, and it was ruled that the Wales international did handle it. Did look very harsh.

Coventry are still in this game but City have their chances to put them away. Enzo was deemed offside when he set up a strike for Haaland. The UK’s most expensive player has got better during this game.

Looks like it will be ruled out for handball.

Vitaly Janelt breaks the deadlock after Brentford were battered in the first half.

Keith Andrews is a brave manager. Having been forced into a change after 17 minutes when his captain, Nathan Collisn was injured, he shook it up at half-time by replacing three of his biggest signings, Kayode, Sangaré and Ouattara for Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony.

There might be a VAR check but Neco Williams is in like Flynn when Tonali makes a bad mistake.

Mohammed Kudus comes on for Sávio and Andy Robertson for Destiny Udogie.

Igor Jesus and Daniel Muñoz come on for Ola Aina and Dan Ndoye.

Tyrick Mitchell has scored his second. What do they say about London buses…

Mitchell rampaging up the left, shoots. It’s blocked by García who tries to clear by hitting it straight into Mitchell’s foot whence it ricochets past Bernd Leno.

It was the culmination of a long passage of huffing and puffing after Marmoush had scudded a free-kick straight into the Forest wall.

Forest are clinging on a bit at the moment with some pretty desperate defending.

It was put in by Jacob Strand Larsen, who came on for Eddie Nketiah at half-time but he was offside.

With Tottenham appearing so toothless in attack, you have to wonder whether Roberto De Zerbi ends the long wait for Mykhailo Mudryk.

It is over 600 days since Mudryk last played a competitive match.

There is also the option of Dominic Solanke on the bench too.

Tanaka was offside when he turned in Stach’s free-kick. Leeds squander opportunity to double their lead.

Because of the 4½ minute VAR check for the Ballard ‘goal’ and an injury to Nathan Collins that forced the Bees’ captain off.

These are clearly two teams in transition.

Tottenham have spent over £300m this summer and are still waiting for lift-off.

Forest are embarking on a new era under Oliver Glasner with a style of play that will take time to implement.

It’s been a messy game so far with both teams struggling to impose themselves.

The best chance fell to one of Tottenham’s new arrivals, Omar Marmoush, but he drilled a shot wide of the post.

Josh King scores one and makes one. César Palacios with the rebound after Gonzalo García’s effort was parried to him.

Oliver Glasner’s wife Bettina is making her first visit to the City Ground today.

Glasner said that he is hoping to celebrate dinner tonight with his first three points since taking charge.

In a ding-dong match, the left-back, Tyrick Mitchell, pounces to fire Palace level.

Lewis Dunk saves Brighton after Calvert-Lewin had rounded Verbruggen and tried to slide it in on the angle.

Erling Haaland at the back post with a thunderous header – his 300th goal in club football.

Kamada was offside by a gnat’s whisker. VAR is making this job ridiculous.

Both Calvert-Lewin and Tanaka should have finished but Bogle was there to make sure. Elvedi spun on to the ball in the right of the penalty area to stand up a left-foot cross to the back post. Calvert-Lewin leapt and powered a low header hat Rushworth scooped out. Tanaka, following up, sliced his shot from five yards across goal where Bogle blindsided a defender to tap it in.

Kamada equalises at the Cottage, played in by an excellent pass from Pino.

Coventry fans are in good voice – and jeering Enzo Fernandez when he gets the ball. The Argentina midfielder has been quiet so far.

Messy start here at the City Ground with both teams struggling for fluency.

Tottenham are still waiting for their first goal of the season with a drastically reshaped team.

Danso was deemed to be interfering with play in an offside position, blocking the goalkeeper’s view of Ballard’s strike.

Disasi gives the ball away to Charles who finds Bobb. His pass sets up King for a shot which is deflected past Henderson.

Kevin Danso was standing in front of Kelleher in an offside position.

Was a Sunderland player blocking the goalkeeper?

Dan Ballard opens the scoring at the GTech from a free-kick.

Cherki makes headway down the left and sends over a dipping, menacing cross towards Enzo who is pushed high as a No10 but Carl Rushworth plucks it out of the air.

It’s Enzo Fernández replacing Nico O’Reilly not Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Enzo Fernandez will start, it has been confirmed, with O’Reilly injured in the warm-up

Fernandez is lined up in the tunnel ready to come out.

England left-back, who was slated to play in midfield, hurt his back/hip in the warm-up.

Seems to have a problem with his lower back or hip. He has been ruled out of the match.

One pleasing thing about the signing of Melvin Bard by Leeds is the prospect of it reviving oft-heard Elland Road shouts from 1989-92 of ‘Giyit Mel’ and ‘G’won Mel’ in encouragement of the sainted Sterland, the Zico of Fullerton Park.

The big headline news from Tottenham is that Mykhailo Mudryk is on the bench.

Signed from Chelsea on deadline day on an initial loan, Mudryk was once branded as a future Ballon d’Or winner by Roberto De Zerbi after they worked together at Shakhtar.

Mudryk has not played a competitive match since November 2024 after being suspended by the Football Association following a positive test for performance-enhancing meldonium.

Enzo Fernández’s record deal to Manchester City was facilitated by English-founded agency Unique Sports Management, it can be revealed.

Fernández sealed a £125m move from Chelsea on deadline day, equalling the UK transfer record of Alexander Isak to Liverpool a year ago.

Football Association documents due to be published later in the season will show Unique to have played their part in the biggest transfer of the summer.

Fernández is represented by The Elegant Game, headed by ex-Argentina international Javier Pastore, although he is not registered with the FA for transfers in England.

Unique, which also represented Anthony Gordon for his move to Barcelona, were brought in to close the deal, which was agreed between clubs on deadline day afternoon.

The English-founded agency have Marc Guéhi, who moved to City in January, on their books and their summer deals included Gordon to Barca, Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea and Taylor Harwood-Bellis to Aston Villa. Troy Parrott, who scored the winner for Real Betis against Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, is also in the Unique stable.

Will this be third time lucky for Tottenham Hotspur after their £300m+ summer reset?

In typical Tottenham fashion, their start to the Premier League season has not been straightforward with two defeats, five goals conceded and none scored so far.

The popular opinion is that it will eventually click, but Tottenham’s supporters are still scarred by those two successive 17th-placed finishes.

Forest have won their last four games against Spurs, so it will be an early sign of promise if Roberto De Zerbi can secure a positive result here.

Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

“Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

“I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just said he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

“I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very important that he is with us.”

Maresca said he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

We have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi plans to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

#1822. Tuttosport: A ‘different story with the starters’ – how Milan’s win in Genoa proved Amorim right

Everyone expected a reaction from AC Milan after their disappointing Europa League defeat to Ferencvaros, and one arrived.

As Tuttosport (via MilanNews) write this morning, Milan did redeem themselves after their dreadful display on Thursday against the Hungarians. It wasn’t an easy match for the Rossoneri, who struggled heavily towards the end and even nearly conceded an equaliser, but they got over the line.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The three golden points not only allows the team to have a bit more of a peaceful international break but it also means that a spot inside the top four has been reclaimed, with Champions League qualification the major objective for 2026-27.

As the paper points out, one thing is quite clear from yesterday’s match: with the ‘starters’ on the pitch, it’s a completely different Milan which displays quality and an identity. It is equally clear that Ruben Amorim was right a few days ago when he declared that with this squad, the Devils can compete for only one competition and not two.

When the Portuguese coach was ‘forced’ to field second string players to manage energy levels, aside from the win against RB Salzburg they suffered only defeats. The difference between starters and alternatives is evident, and is also evidenced by the fact that yesterday the Milan team struggled towards the end when Amorim was forced to make some substitutions.

After the match, the head coach was once again asked about the topic of effective rotation, addressing the differences in Milan’s performance between Serie A and the Europa League.

“Rotation is necessary for us. Clearly, it was a bad match on Thursday for the players we have: I think it’s a mentality issue, and we have to address it,” he said.

“The only way I know is to work, train with the players, explain, show videos, because there were some things so obvious that I don’t need to explain. I’ll just show some clips of the match and they’ll understand.

“I’m satisfied with the evolution we’re having. We’re completely changing our way of playing. We have more ball possession. We control games with the ball more. I think we’ve had some moments during these matches, really good moments with a good culture. I think we’re far from the end.

“I think we lack time in the final third of the pitch. We control the ball away from the opponent’s area. This is also a key point for Goncalo Ramos to have more clear-cut chances. It’s clearly not Goncalo’s fault. Pulisic is away from the area. Gonçalo is far from the penalty area.

“All these players play far from the penalty area, so I can say we’re still far from the final product, because we’re still working on good progression, but then in the final third of the pitch we waste a lot of time with the ball there.”

#1821. Armenia vs Cyprus - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 10 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 10:19

Armenia welcome Cyprus to the Vazgen Sargsyan Republican Stadium on Thursday evening for their penultimate League C fixture in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, the Collectives played out a goalless draw with Montenegro at the Podgorica City Stadium, while the Blue and Whites claimed a narrow 2-1 victory over Latvia in Nicosia.

After just missing out on promotion to League B in the 2024-25 campaign, finishing second in their group but falling to a thumping 9-1 aggregate defeat against Georgia in the promotion playoff, Armenia will have mixed feelings about how they have started their latest Nations League endeavours.

Despite starting their campaign on the front foot with a 2-0 victory over Latvia in Yerevan, the Collectives have since suffered defeats to Montenegro and Cyprus, although a goalless draw against the former in early October has just about kept Thursday’s hosts in contention for promotion from League C.

With two group matches remaining, Eghishe Melikyan’s men sit third in their respective group, though currently loitering three points below Cyprus in the table, Armenia almost certainly need to claim victory this week if they want any chance of progressing through to a playoff tie.

To do so, the Collectives will certainly have to be better than their recent form suggests too, as despite never before losing a home match against Cyprus, Armenia have claimed victory over the Blue and Whites in just one of their prior eight meetings.

Following a bitterly disappointing World Cup qualifying campaign, winning just one of their six matches to finish fourth in European Group H and sit five points below Romania in the playoff places, Cyprus will be content with how they have bounced back in their latest Nations League efforts.

Although they failed to win either of their first two competition outings, losing to Montenegro in their opening fixture before playing out a stalemate with Latvia, the Blue and Whites have truly kick-started their promotion bid by claiming back-to-back victories and as a result sit in a promising position with just a pair of group matches remaining.

Heading into Thursday’s contest, Apostolos Mantzios’s side sit second in their group with a comfortable cushion over third-placed Armenia, but with Montenegro only three points ahead at the summit, Cyprus still have the opportunity to secure automatic promotion rather than a playoff place, providing plenty of incentive to extend their winning streak through to the end of the campaign.

Having won three of their previous five encounters with Armenia, including a 2-0 victory when the nations met at the GSP Stadium earlier on in the campaign, the Blue and Whites will certainly be confident that they can close down on top spot this week too and craft another chance at winning their place in League B.

Armenia will be without Eduard Spertsyan for Thursday’s contest after the midfielder recently picked up an Achilles tendon injury, while backup goalkeeper Henri Avagyan has also been ruled out.

Sergey Muradyan, Julio Bueno and Sunderland’s Finn Geragusyan round off the hosts’ injury list, though the Collectives are also missing Erik Simonyan, Kamo Hovhannisyan and Vahan Bichakhchyan from the latest squad selection due to a lack of match fitness.

With Henrikh Mkhitaryan retiring from international football in 2022 and Spertsyan out injured, Melikyan’s biggest goal threat on Thursday could well be Tenerife forward Grant-Leon Ranos, who is likely to lead the line for Armenia.

Cyprus are missing both Giannis Satsias and Konstantinos Sotiriou as the pair continue their recovery from muscle issues, while Omonia forward Andronikos Kakoullis remains sidelined with an undisclosed problem.

The Blue and Whites’ only other injury woe is Pafos goalkeeper Charalampos Kyriakidis, who suffered an arm issue in June, though the visitors will also be without Kostas Pileas after the 27-year-old full-back received a red card in last month’s meeting with Armenia.

Having already netted two goals in the current Nations League campaign, Burnley forward Marcus Edwards is undoubtedly Mantzios’s dangerman and is almost certain to start in midfield just behind Ioannis Pittas on Thursday.

Beglaryan; Piloyan, Simonyan, Harutyunyan, Tiknizyan; Iwu, K.Hovhannisyan; Serobyan, Manvelyan, N.Hovhannisyan, Ranos

Fabiano; Konomis, Kyprianou, Panagiotou, Malekkidis; Artymatas, Kastanos; Edwards, Loizou, Georgiou; Pittas

With their form slipping in recent matches and a gap beginning to open up between themselves and the promotion places, it is imperative that Armenia claim all three points against Cyprus if they are to have even the slightest chance of competing in League B when the 2028-29 Nations League campaign gets underway.

However, with the Blue and Whites enjoying a promising run of form and also chasing down Montenegro in the race for automatic promotion, we believe Armenia’s hopes of progressing will run their course on Thursday as the visitors to take all three points in Yerevan.

#1820. Tuchel not eyeing club return amid Pochettino Man Utd links

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Thomas Tuchel insists he will not leave the England job to take any offer in club football before Euro 2028, amid reports that Mauricio Pochettino is set to leave the United States for Manchester United.

On Wednesday, widespread reports suggested Pochettino – who has been in charge of the USMNT since 2024 – was set to quit his role and join United.

The Red Devils are set to sack Michael Carrick after entering the international break 18th in the Premier League table, the first time they have sat in the relegation zone this far into a season since 1986-87.

And ahead of England facing Croatia and Spain in the Nations League, that impending move led reporters to ask how Tuchel sees his future.

In February, the German penned a two-year contract extension to cover England's home campaign at Euro 2028.

He attracted stern criticism following the Three Lions' World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina in July, but the Football Association reiterated its commitment to him after the tournament.

Asked if he had a release clause or would push for an exit for the right opportunity, Tuchel said: "There's no release clause, and there's no intention.

"I signed the contract – I want to stay until the Euros. I want to do the Euros. We have unfinished business."

Asked if he could guarantee he would not leave his current job, even if one of Europe's top clubs came calling, Tuchel replied: "Yeah, I would say so."

Next up: Croatia  Returning to @wembleystadium for more UEFA Nations League action!  #ThreeLions | @EASPORTSFC https://t.co/aZVmRxbfrn

However, when Euro 2028 is finished, the former Borussia Dortmund, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and Bayern Munich boss intends to return to club football.

"I miss the 50 matches [a year], as I said. I miss those two minutes when everything is done," Tuchel said.

"You go out two minutes before the whistle goes, it's the best two minutes, everything is done, and you're in a full stadium, the lights are on and you're just so excited and you're part of it.

"Those are actually the two minutes where I realise how lucky and how grateful I am, and then the whistle goes and you're just in the tunnel again and you're trying to win the game for your team. And you do that every four days."

Since Tuchel's first game in charge, England have won more games than any other European nation (20), while only Belgium have equalled their 65 goals.

Tuchel’s 20 wins in 26 matches also represents the fastest any Three Lions manager has reached 20 victories.

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:16, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:52

Real Madrid midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni has withdrawn from Zinedine Zidane's France squad due to injury.

France are preparing to conclude the first phase of the Nations League with an away game against Italy on Thursday and a home meeting with Turkey on Sunday.

Zidane's side are currently sitting top of the standings after collecting 10 points from their opening four games, although they still have work to do to secure a quarter-final spot.

If they are to seal a last eight berth, France will have to do it without the services of Real Madrid's Tchouameni, who has been forced to pull out of the squad with a muscular injury.

In a statement released on Tuesday evening, the French Football Federation said: “Aurelien Tchouameni is once again experiencing discomfort in his right adductor, as he did last summer during the World Cup.

"He has been dealing with this discomfort since arriving at the French National Football Centre in Clairefontaine.

"After taking his medical history into account and holding a conversation just minutes ago with Real Madrid’s medical staff, the French national team’s medical department, in agreement with the player, has decided to release him to his club.

"He will spend tonight with the squad before returning to Madrid tomorrow.”

The FFF also confirmed that no replacement will be called up, leaving Zidane with Eduardo Camavinga, Warren Zaire-Emery, Adrien Rabiot and Lucas Da Cunha as his central midfield options.

Tchouameni, who also missed the last international window, will have to wait until at least March to make his first appearance under Zidane.

Meanwhile, his latest setback will concern Real Madrid, especially as it appears to be a similar issue to the one that forced him to miss the start of the season.

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho will certainly hope the issue is a minor one, having relied heavily on Tchouameni over the last couple of months.

Los Blancos will return to action against Celta Vigo on November 11 before they face PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League just a few days later.

#1818. MN: Hostile welcome, Amorim’s avoidance, De Rossi’s praise – behind the scenes of the win in Genoa

Some of the unseen details from AC Milan’s win away against Genoa have emerged, ranging from hostility to strong praise.

Goals from Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic inside the opening 20 minutes would be enough for Milan, who were nonetheless left clinging on in the final stages after Ellertsson’s goal. MilanNews have revealed some of the behind-the-scenes moments from the Marassi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The day in Genoa wasn’t exactly a walk in the park. First and foremost, there was the rather hostile atmosphere created by the Genoa fans towards the Rossoneri. This forced the relevant authorities to ban all residents of Lombardy from attending.

Milan fan groups weren’t even allowed to go to the Aquarium in Genoa’s Porto Antico. It is a shame for so many reasons, and one that reflects the complicated state under which Italian football still operates.

However, there were still Milanisti there to support the team and they made their voices heard. At the end of the match, both Goncalo Ramos and Diego Moreira gave their shirts to young fans in the away sector.

The game could have been a totally different story had it not been for Davide Massa’s controversial decision. At start of the second half, Adrien Rabiot stole the ball, was racing alone toward the penalty area with Cisse to his left, and was fouled by Marcandalli.

Despite the fact it was a clear last-man challenge, he was not sent off. When asked Amorim about yesterday’s specific incident and the refereeing method in general in the press conference, the Portuguese coach responded with a laugh, a smile and a grimace.

It was as if to say: “I’d like to say something, but it’s better if I don’t.” His public response went along this path: “I won’t comment on it, you have the match, because I know that talking about referees isn’t something that could help my team. I just want to help my team, so I won’t say anything about the referees.”

Speaking of press conferences, Daniele De Rossi’s thoughts on Amorim and Modric were very interesting: “I shouldn’t judge Amorim. He’s younger than me, but he has a lot more experience than me. I learn from him. We study him, we watch him. He plays with a system that I really like.

“He puts a lot of quality on the wings, something I’ve also tried to do here. Certainly not Moreira, but with the right proportions and possibilities. I like the way he communicates; he doesn’t blame his players even when he loses, he’s always honest when he loses. He’s doing a great job.

“For anyone who loves this sport, it’s exciting to see Modric play football like this at 41. Last year I had him man-marked, this year he played with two. He has more playing time. Maybe he plays a little slower, but the idea is there.

“We clashed a couple of times and I told him, ‘I don’t play anymore so I can’t beat you up.’ But he’s great, really great. He’s like Rabiot: world-class players. Really beautiful.”

#1817. 'Winning at the Emirates is very hard... but we were a team of warriors': Hull City hero GEOVANNI on his iconic goal against Arsenal, why it very nearly never happened and why the Tigers 'will always be in my heart'

Published: 21:00 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 06:07 EST, 7 November 2026

The greatest moment in Hull City's Premier League history began with Geovanni trying to go home.

'I was ill all night, I barely slept at all,' says Geovanni, who was gripped by a fever and thumping headache less than 24 hours before he was due to walk out at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium in September 2008. The Brazilian rang his wife from the team hotel to tell her he was coming home and planned to have someone pick him up.

Thankfully, his wife Roberta would not hear of it.

'God really used her that day,' he tells Daily Mail Sport. 'She said: "Geovanni, stay there, God will honour you. Hang on and tomorrow try to get a bit of sleep."'

When Hull staff came to his room the next morning, he asked to be left to sleep. He dosed up on medicine and went for lunch, but sat out the light pre-match training session with his temperature touching 38 degrees Celsius.

'And then I got to that game, which was so spectacular,' he says, 'and I was able to score and help Hull beat Arsenal.'

Geovanni unleashes a spectacular equaliser for Hull at the Emirates Stadium back in September 2008

The goal inspired a famous comeback win for the Tigers, who became only the second team to win away at Arsenal

It was Hull's first league meeting with Arsenal for 93 years, in the first top-flight season of the club's then 104-year history.

Arsene Wenger's side had started the day top of the table and Paul McShane's own goal put Arsenal ahead after 51 minutes. Most expected the floodgates to open.

But 11 minutes later up stepped Hull's brilliant Brazilian, a marquee signing from Manchester City in the summer of 2008 after the Tigers' unexpected promotion.

Geovanni cut inside Theo Walcott and sent a 25-yard rocket into Manuel Almunia's top corner. Daniel Cousin headed in a historic winner four minutes later and Hull became only the second side to beat Arsenal at the Emirates.

'Beating Arsenal at the Emirates is very hard, and we pulled it off,' says Geovanni, now 46, speaking from his home in Brazil. 'That was a team of warriors, great players, and we had a really good friendship. And that day we walked away with a great win.'

On Saturday, Hull return to the Emirates to face the champions and league leaders. The Tigers are 11th after nine games. It is a strong start that few predicted.

'Hull have to give 100 per cent, the maximum, be switched on the whole time,' says Geovanni. 'It's difficult, but it's not impossible, because Hull really did beat Arsenal.'

Eight days after the Emirates match, Geovanni did it again. A stunning 30-yard free-kick at White Hart Lane nestled into the top corner past his friend and compatriot Heurelho Gomes.

'We beat Tottenham with Gareth Bale, Luka Modric, all those players,' he says. 'For me, those two are top-drawer. They're two great players who left a mark on me.'

The win moved Hull into third and by the end of October they were level on points at the top. 'London 0 Hull 2' read the headline in the local paper, in reference to Hull band The Housemartins' 1986 album London 0 Hull 4, as the city revelled in its newfound fame.

Geovanni (centre) was part of another iconic Premier League moment, when Phil Brown gave his team a public dressing down at half-time of a loss at Manchester City

The Brazilian returned to Hull's MKM Stadium last year and received a hero's welcome

Geovanni took centre stage. Arriving on a free that summer after being released by Manchester City, he credits manager Phil Brown and assistant Brian Horton for giving him a second chance in the Premier League.

'They were very special people in allowing me to stay in England, which was my dream,' he says. 'And I learned a lot from both of them. Brian was a very experienced coach, he played for Hull, he managed there, so the affection and respect are huge. Whenever I can talk about them, I do.

'In the first year, Hull surprised a lot of people precisely because of the way we played. Sometimes we'd start in a 4-3-1-2, I played as the No10 behind two strikers. And if we were struggling to mark, I'd drop in to close down the left flank and we'd go back to a 4-4-2.'

The dressing room did the rest. Richard Garcia, an Australian winger with Uruguayan parents, helped translate team talks from English into Spanish and captain Ian Ashbee, Nicky Barmby and Bernard Mendy all made Geovanni feel welcome. 'I'm really happy about the friendships I made in that dressing room,' he says.

Geovanni was part of another of the Premier League's most iconic moments, when he and his team-mates received a public dressing down from his manager on the pitch at half-time of a 5-1 loss to Manchester City on Boxing Day 2008. Eleven months later, Jimmy Bullard scored a penalty before recreating the telling off in celebration.

'It was good for breaking the ice,' says Geovanni. 'From that day on the atmosphere got better too, because we can all make mistakes. The most important thing is to admit the mistake and move on.'

Geovanni's finest moment for Manchester City, with whom he spent one season after stints with Barcelona, Benfica and Cruzeiro, came in the Manchester derby, where he was called into the side by manager Sven-Goran Eriksson because Stephen Ireland was ill.

'He called me over and said, "Geovanni, this game... are you ready?". That was the best news I'd had all day, knowing I was going to start.' The day did, in fact, get better. Geovanni scored the only goal in a 1-0 victory.

Geovanni smashes home a winner for City in the Manchester derby, a year before his move to Hull

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages

He struck again against United in November 2008, in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford

United were a familiar victim. In December 2005, his diving header for Benfica helped knock Sir Alex Ferguson's side out of the Champions League in the group stages, while he also scored in a 4-3 defeat for Hull at Old Trafford in 2008.

'A player has to turn up in the big games,' he says. 'United were a machine back then: Giggs, Paul Scholes, Gary Neville, Anderson, Ronaldo, Rooney.'

Geovanni's greatest regret, though, remains that he didn't heed the advice of Barca boss Louis van Gaal, who wanted to turn the wannabe striker into a wing-back.

He reflects: 'If I could go back in time, I'd listen to what Van Gaal said, because it would have been easier for me to fight for a place at wing-back than as a striker, where there were great players: Javier Saviola, Rivaldo, Patrick Kluivert, Marc Overmars.'

Luiz Felipe Scolari, his coach at Cruzeiro, gave him his only senior Brazil cap, against Mexico at the 2001 Copa America. 'It was a dream for me: to leave a town of 4,000 people (Acaiaca) and one day represent Brazil,' he says. 'He (Scolari) was a father to me.'

These days Geovanni is a volunteer pastor in Belo Horizonte and runs a players' agency with his father-in-law and an old youth-team friend.

But Hull will always be in his heart. He has a picture of himself in a Hull shirt in his house and received a hero's return after heading back to the city last year.

'I love them (the fans). I have a very special affection for the Hull supporters,' he says. 'It was two years in which I gave everything. I went back there last year and was really well received, it was great: friends from my time there, the fans too.

Battling Blackburn's Damien Duff in a pre-season friendly in his Barcelona days. He spent only two seasons with the Catalan club, having left Cruzeiro to move to Europe

'I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart'

'And I know I left my mark on the club's history. Whenever people talk about Hull City, about Brazilians, they'll remember Geovanni, the time I spent there, the feats we achieved together.

'And I believe I gave those fans a lot of joy, in games that seemed impossible. God blessed me and I was able to score goals and bring joy to that city. I'm very grateful for everything they did for me. Hull and the fans will always be in my heart.

'My two years at Hull were perhaps the two most special years for me. The sweetest spell of my career.'

By Ben Sully | 11 Nov 2026 00:56, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 01:05

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk insists he is "not in any panic" over his contract situation at Anfield.

The Netherlands international has been one of Liverpool's star players since he arrived from Southampton in the summer of 2018.

Van Dijk has made 389 appearances for the Reds, helping the club win multiple pieces of silverware, including two Premier League titles and a Champions League crown.

While he may not be at the age of 35, Van Dijk continues to play a prominent role for the Merseyside club, having started 14 of the club's 16 competitive matches this season.

As it stands, it is unclear if this is the final season of his successful Liverpool career, with his current deal set to expire at the end of the campaign.

Van Dijk has now issued an update on his contract situation, explaining that he is not stressing about his uncertain Anfield future.

“I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing, so let’s see what the season brings,” Van Dijk told reporters.

“I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case.

"If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.

“I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. I’m not in any panic whatsoever.”

With Van Dijk set to turn 36 next summer, there will be an obvious temptation to look to the long-term future and sign a younger defender who could fill Van Dijk's boots for years to come.

However, the Dutchman is still continuing to perform at a high level and has formed a strong central defensive partnership with Jeremy Jacquet this term.

In the short term, Van Dijk's current focus will be on returning to full fitness after withdrawing from Xavi's Netherlands squad with a minor issue.

Manchester United have reportedly considered new coaching support as a potential option should they decide against sacking Michael Carrick.

Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada will hold a crucial meeting with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe in Monaco on Wednesday.

Carrick's future will be the main topic of discussion, with Wilcox and Berrada expected to recommend a change of head coach.

Instead of sacking their current head coach, Man United's decision-makers could look to add coaching staff to Carrick's backroom team.

Suffering an infamous World Cup collapse back in July as they watched their North American adventure come to an end thanks to a rollercoaster 3-2 loss against Argentina, Egypt are searching for some recent stability. Putting a maiden AFCON qualifying victory on the board as they signed off September with a dominant 5-0 victory away at South Sudan, Egypt will be seeking a repeat performance here. While the African heavyweights might be searching for some recent stability, they have certainly been handed a golden opportunity this weekend. Rightfully installed as a landslide contender when they return to Cairo on Friday night, Egypt also hold a dominant record against Malawi. Landing a routine 4-0 win when they last met Malawi back in March 2023, we are expecting a similar outcome.

#1812. New Zealand vs India - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 11 Nov 2026 02:09, Last updated: 11 Nov 2026 05:00

India are set for a tough test on Thursday, when they travel to Auckland's Go Media Stadium for an international friendly against New Zealand, marking their first-ever visit to the country.

The All Whites are hoping to bounce back from defeat last time out, while the Blue Tigers are looking to follow the winning example set by their alternative squad at the SAFF Championship.

Darren Bazeley's New Zealand followed up their group-stage elimination from World Cup 2026 with a three-game unbeaten run, drawing 2-2 with Palestine before triumphing 3-0 against China and on penalties against Panama during the last international break.

However, the All Whites' streak came to an end on October 5, when they were downed 2-1 by Japan in the final of the friendly Kirin Cup.

Captain Chris Wood - the nation's record scorer and appearance holder - assisted Ben Old's equaliser that day, but he was unable to respond when Ritsu Doan netted the winner for the Samurai Blue four minutes after his second-half substitution.

Looking ahead to Thursday, the hosts have never lost to India, most recently running out 2-1 winners in the friendly AIFF Intercontinental Cup in June 2018.

However, this week's clash will be just the second time they have faced the visitors this century, and only the third meeting between the sides throughout history, after first locking horns during a goalless draw in the 1981 edition of the Merdeka Tournament.

New Zealand (ranked 88th) are the favourites to come out on top due to their 50-superior placement in FIFA's ranking system, though fans may still be cautious considering that Bazeley's team have lost two of their last three matches on home turf.

Meanwhile, Khalid Jamil's India arrive as underdogs but are keen to test their mettle in a pair of fixtures against an opponent who qualified for the World Cup.

Thursday's friendly in Auckland and Sunday's follow up in Christchurch come as part of a celebration marking 100 years of sporting connection between the nations, and the Blue Tigers' manager called for fans to join them on matchday in his press conference.

“I know there are many Indian fans here in New Zealand - I would request them to come to the stadium and support the team. Their support is important for us, and we will try to give our best on the pitch,” said Jamil.

Another challenge facing the visitors is the fact they are split across two squads, one that is set to take part in these friendlies and another that is currently contesting the 2026 SAFF Championship, the latter of which beat Pakistan 3-2 on November 5.

Beyond that victory by their alternative side, India are heading into this clash on the back of a seven-game winless run in friendlies, including a 6-1 thrashing by Uruguay and a 4-0 hammering by Brazil last month.

New Zealand International Friendlies form:

New Zealand are without right-back Callan Elliot through injury, but the versatile Bill Tuiloma could feature in his absence, joining Nando Pijnaker, Tyler Bindon and James McGarry in defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, Chris Wood looks set to lead the line, supported from out wide by Dundee United's Jesse Randall and 20-year-old Nathan Walker of Wellington Phoenix, who could make his All Whites debut.

As for India, they have left experienced goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu out of the squad, while centre-back Anwar Ali is sidelined due to a hamstring injury.

With that in mind, Vishal Kaith is likely to start between the sticks on Thursday, shielded by a pairing of Bijoy Varghese and Mehtab Singh.

The Blue Tigers are also without midfielder Lalengmawia Ralte, who is known as Apuia, though Anirudh Thapa could be joined by Lalrinliana Hnamte in the visitors' double pivot.

Paulsen; Tuiloma, Pijnaker, Bindon, McGarry; Rufer; Randall, Garbett, Bayliss, Walker; Wood

Kaith; Singh Tekcham, Varghese, Me Singh, Mishra; Hnamte, Thapa; Ma Singh, Williams, Kuruniyan; Lalhlansanga

New Zealand are the overwhelming favourites despite featuring a number of young players in their squad, and they will be hoping to deliver a strong showing on home soil.

India will arrive knowing that they are likely to be on the losing side, but that underdog status could inspire them to find the back of the net at least once on Thursday.

#1811. Rabiot hits out at refereeing after Marcandalli incident: “Constantly lying won’t achieve progress”

Adrien Rabiot has had his say on the incident that happened during AC Milan’s win over Genoa, in which he was brought down through on goal.

The controversial moment everyone is talking about came early in the second half. Rabiot pressured Marcandalli and stole the ball off him and he was about to surge into Genoa’s half, with only Alphadjo Cisse to his left for company in a two-on-zero breakaway.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Marcandalli hauled him down, yet the referee Davide Massa only saw fit to award a yellow card, and the VAR chief did not deem it necessary to call him over to the monitor for another look. Milan won anyway in the end, but it would have been a totally different game had that been given.

Former referee Gianpaolo Calvarese commented on the incident on his Instagram page and he described Marcandalli’s yellow card as a ‘fair’ decision, which prompted Rabiot to respond in the comments.

“In life, as in football, you can make mistakes. You have to at least be able to admit them. Constantly lying won’t achieve progress, and Italian football is the one that suffers the consequences. Think about it. Bonne soirée,” the Frenchman said.

A post shared by Gianpaolo Calvarese (@gianpaolocalvarese_official)

The relationship between Rabiot and Italian referees has always been characterised by a direct, unfiltered approach. The former PSG man has never been one to hide when he feels he’s suffered an injustice.

He demonstrated this during his time at Juventus. In April 2022, after the defeat against Inter he wrote on Instagram: “It’s difficult to play with 11 against 12.” A year later, in Juventus-Sevilla, he protested again over a denied penalty, even showing the media the marks left by the studs on his leg.

Rabiot brought this to Milan too. After the match against Atalanta on October 18th, for example, he questioned the awarding of bookings, complaining about several uncalled fouls, leading to his famous celebration in front of Chiffi when he scored the 2-0 goal.

#1810. Guatemala vs Canada - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 11 Nov 2026 02:46

Making their first appearance in the quarter-finals of the CONCACAF Nations League, Guatemala will host Canada in the opening leg of that tie on Friday at Estadio El Trebol in Guatemala City.

A 1-0 win over Suriname helped the Guatemalans top Group B with seven points, while Canada are one of the top four ranked teams in CONCACAF, earning a bye into the knockout stage as a result.

It was a roller coaster of a group stage for Guatemala, but fortunately for them it ended with the Central Americans at the top.

Luis Fernando Tena’s men opened that phase by conceding an injury-time goal in a defeat to Jamaica (3-2) but ended it with an stoppage-time winner versus Suriname.

That victory vaulted them into the Nations League knockout stage for the first time, scoring nine goals along the way, the joint-most for them ever in the League A group phase.

Unfortunately though it came at a cost as the coach will be missing some players for this match due to the post-match altercations in that outing.

Since their heartbreaking defeat on matchday one to the Jamaicans, Guatemala have collected a clean sheet in their last three Nations League affairs, having conceded a combined 14 goals this year before this tournament began.

In their six previous League A encounters at home, this team have yet to lose, while conceding a mere two goals overall during that stretch.

Los Chapines can stretch their unbeaten run against Canada to three matches across all competitions, eliminating them on penalties in the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup quarter-finals.

Following their historic run to the last 16 of the World Cup last summer, the Canadians had a solid fall international window.

Jesse Marsch’s men won two of their three friendlies in that window, collecting two clean sheets along the way.

On Friday, they will hope to avoid consecutive international defeats for the first time since the 2024 Copa America, after losing their last international outing to the USA (1-0).

The Canucks boast a 100% away record in the quarter-finals of this tournament, winning at Jamaica in 2023 (2-1) and blanking Suriname on the road a year later (1-0).

They have won their last four internationals when netting the opening goal and have never lost a knockout match in this competition as the visiting team.

Friday will be their second Nations League match on Central American soil, with Les Rouges losing the previous one in the group stage at Honduras in 2022 (2-1).

Because of a post-match confrontation against Suriname, Jonathan Franco and Carlos Estrada will be suspended for three matches, while Oscar Santis is out due to a hamstring strain.

Matt Evans netted in the 96th minute to earn them a place in the knockout stage of this competition, his first goal on the international stage, and Nicholas Hagen collected two clean sheets in the group phase.

Canadian captain Alphonso Davies is reportedly ready to play according to Marsch, though Jonathan Osorio and Jacob Shaffelburg withdrew with injuries, while Cyle Larin was not selected because of back irritation.

Davies can move into a tie for ninth in all-time international goals Friday, while Richie Laryea will draw even with Paul Stalteri for sixth in all-time caps with his next one.

Hagen; Herrera, Yanes, Samayoa, Morales; Lopez, Castellanos, Rosales, Escobar, Rubin, Lom

Crepeau; Laryea, De Fougeroles, Ivanisevic, Davies; Buchanan, Saliba, Choiniere, Millar; J. David, Oluwaseyi

Even with Davies back, the environment in Guatemala will be difficult for the visitors to navigate, and we expect the Central Americans’ suffocating defence to limit the scoring chances for Canada.

Enjoying what has become a breakout campaign with Bundesliga outfit RB Leipzig this season, Nusa finds his stock at a red-hot high.

Now in his third campaign at the Red Bull Arena, Nusa has quickly blossomed into one of Europe’s hottest young attacking starlets and is reportedly attracting plenty of heavyweight interest from across the continent.

Along with notching a consolation Champions League strike during Leipzig’s 3-2 defeat against Manchester City earlier in the month, the 21-year-old is enjoying a sensational domestic flurry.

In his nine Bundesliga appearances so far this season, the former Club Brugge starlet has registered 11 direct goal contributions (four goals, seven assists).

🚨 Arsenal face a difficult task signing Antonio Nusa in January, with RB Leipzig under no financial pressure to sell.

#1808. Arsenal teach Chelsea a lesson in how to be champions

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

The chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his new club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

Morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm

Instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

This was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

In fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be said that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

“Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

For the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN

Chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

Ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

“It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

“It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher says Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr

“I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”

“It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We showed our quality today. The result reflected that.”

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”

“We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”
